title.zh: 卷一百四十五 志第九十八 儀衞三
title.raw: 卷一百四十五 志第九十八 儀衞三 Volume 145 Treatises 98: Ceremonial Guards 3

sentences.zh: 儀衛三○國初鹵簿

translations.literal: Ceremonial Guards 3 ○ Imperial Procession Insignia at the Founding of the Dynasty
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial Guards, Part 3: Imperial Procession Insignia in the Early Dynasty

sentences.zh: 國初鹵簿。

translations.literal: Imperial procession insignia at the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial procession insignia in the early dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆四年，將郊祀，大禮使範質與鹵簿使張昭、儀仗使劉溫叟，同詳定大駕鹵簿之制，惟得唐長興《南郊鹵簿字圖》，校以令文，頗有闊略違戾者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, when a suburban sacrifice was imminent, Grand Ceremony Commissioner Fan Zhi, together with Procession Insignia Commissioner Zhang Zhao and Ceremonial Arms Commissioner Liu Wensou, jointly worked out the regulations for the great imperial procession insignia. They had only the Tang Changxing Diagram of Characters for the Southern Suburb Procession Insignia, and when they checked it against the current statutes, there were many gaps and contradictions.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jianlong era (963), as Emperor Taizu prepared for a suburban sacrifice, Grand Ceremony Commissioner Fan Zhi joined Procession Insignia Commissioner Zhang Zhao and Ceremonial Arms Commissioner Liu Wensou in drafting regulations for the great imperial procession. Their only guide was the Tang Changxing-era Diagram of Characters for the Southern Suburb Procession Insignia, and when they compared it with current statutes, they found many gaps and contradictions.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使陶穀建議：「金吾及諸衛將軍導駕及押仗，舊服紫衣，請依《開元禮》各服本色繡袍。

translations.literal: Rites Commissioner Tao Gu proposed: "The Golden Guard and the generals of the various guards who lead the imperial carriage and supervise the arms escort formerly wore purple robes. We request that, in accordance with the Kaiyuan Rites, each wear embroidered robes in his proper service color.
translations.idiomatic: Rites Commissioner Tao Gu proposed: "The Golden Guard and the generals of the various guards who lead the imperial carriage and supervise the arms escort have long worn purple robes. We ask that, following the Kaiyuan Rites, each instead wear an embroidered robe in his proper service color.

sentences.zh: 金吾以辟邪，左右衛以瑞馬，驍衛以雕虎，威衛以赤豹，武衛以瑞鷹，領軍衛以白澤，監門衛以師子，千牛衛以犀牛，六軍以孔雀為文。

translations.literal: The Golden Guard with the ward-off-evil beast, the Left and Right Guards with the auspicious horse, the Valiant Guard with the carved tiger, the Awesome Guard with the red leopard, the Martial Guard with the auspicious hawk, the Army-leading Guard with the white ze, the Gate-keeping Guard with the lion, the Thousand-Ox Guard with the rhinoceros, and the Six Armies with the peacock as their emblems.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Guard would bear the ward-off-evil beast, the Left and Right Guards the auspicious horse, the Valiant Guard a carved tiger, the Awesome Guard a red leopard, the Martial Guard an auspicious hawk, the Army-leading Guard the white ze, the Gate-keeping Guard a lion, the Thousand-Ox Guard a rhinoceros, and the Six Armies a peacock.

sentences.zh: 舊，執仗軍士悉衣五色畫衣，隨人數給之，無有準式，請以五行相生之色為次，黑衣先之，青衣次之，赤、黃、白又次之。

translations.literal: Formerly, all soldiers bearing arms wore five-colored painted garments issued according to head count, with no fixed standard. It was requested that the colors follow the sequence of the Five Phases generating one another: black garments first, then green, then red, yellow, and white in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, every arms-bearing soldier wore painted garments in five colors, issued according to head count without any fixed standard. Tao Gu asked that the colors follow the generating sequence of the Five Phases: black first, then green, then red, yellow, and white.

sentences.zh: 大駕五輅，各有副車，近代浸廢，請依令文增造。

translations.literal: The five chariots of the great imperial carriage each had an attendant chariot; in recent times this had gradually fallen into disuse. It was requested that they be newly made in accordance with the statutory text.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five chariots in the great imperial train once had an attendant chariot, but this practice had gradually lapsed in recent times. He asked that they be built anew according to statute.

sentences.zh: 又案明宗舊圖，導駕三引而儀仗法物人數多，周太祖鹵簿六引而人數少，請準令文用六引，其鹵簿各依本品以給。」

translations.literal: Further, upon examining the old diagram from Emperor Mingzong of Tang, the leading of the imperial carriage had three sections but the ceremonial arms and ritual objects had many personnel; under Emperor Taizu of Zhou the procession insignia had six sections but fewer personnel. It was requested that six sections be used in accordance with the statutory text, with each item of procession insignia supplied according to its proper grade."
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that under the Tang Emperor Mingzong's old diagram, the imperial escort used three sections but employed many men for ceremonial arms and ritual objects, whereas under the Zhou Emperor Taizu the procession used six sections with fewer men. He proposed adopting six sections as the statute prescribed, with each item of procession insignia supplied according to its proper grade."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 舊清遊隊有甲騎具裝，亡其制度，穀以其所記造之。

translations.literal: The old Pure Excursion Detachment had armored cavalry in full equipment, but its regulations had been lost. Gu had them made according to his records.
translations.idiomatic: The old Pure Excursion Detachment had included armored cavalry in full kit, but its regulations had been lost. Gu had new equipment made according to his own records.

sentences.zh: 又作大輦，皆率意定其制。

translations.literal: He also made a great imperial palanquin, determining its design entirely as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: He also designed a great imperial palanquin, setting its specifications largely on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 穀又取天文大角、攝提列星之象，作攝提旗及北斗旗、二十八宿旗、十二辰旗、龍墀十三旗、五方神旗、五方鳳旗、四瀆旗。

translations.literal: Gu further took the astral images of the Great Horn and the Lodestar constellations and made the Lodestar Banner, the Northern Dipper Banner, the Twenty-eight Lunar Mansions Banner, the Twelve Branches Banner, the Thirteen Dragon Court Banners, the Five Directions Spirit Banners, the Five Directions Phoenix Banners, and the Four Rivers Banners.
translations.idiomatic: Gu also drew on the astral figures of the Great Horn and the Lodestar constellations to create the Lodestar Banner, the Northern Dipper Banner, banners for the twenty-eight lunar mansions and the twelve earthly branches, the thirteen Dragon Court banners, the Five Directions spirit and phoenix banners, and the Four Rivers banners.

sentences.zh: 時有貢黃鸚鵡、白兔，及馴象自來，又作金鸚鵡、玉兔、馴象旗。

translations.literal: At that time there were tribute offerings of a yellow parrot and a white hare, and a tame elephant came of its own accord. He also made Golden Parrot, Jade Hare, and Tame Elephant banners.
translations.idiomatic: When a yellow parrot and a white hare were presented as tribute and a tame elephant arrived on its own, he added Golden Parrot, Jade Hare, and Tame Elephant banners as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖又詔別造大黃龍負圖旗一，大神旗六，日旗一，月旗一，君王萬歲旗一，天下太平旗一，師子旗二，金鸞旗一，金鳳旗一，五龍旗五，凡二十一旗，皆有架，南郊用之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu also ordered separately made one Great Yellow Dragon Bearing the Chart Banner, six Great Spirit Banners, one Sun Banner, one Moon Banner, one Myriad Years to the Sovereign Banner, one All Under Heaven at Peace Banner, two Lion Banners, one Golden Luan Banner, one Golden Phoenix Banner, and five Five-Dragon Banners—in all twenty-one banners, each with a stand, for use at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu further ordered twenty-one additional banners, each mounted on a stand for use at the southern suburb: one Great Yellow Dragon Bearing the Chart banner, six Great Spirit banners, and one each of the Sun, Moon, Myriad Years to the Sovereign, and All Under Heaven at Peace banners, plus two Lion banners, one Golden Luan, one Golden Phoenix, and five Five-Dragon banners.

sentences.zh: 大黃龍負圖旗陳於明德門前，餘二十旗悉立於宿頓宮前，遇朝會冊禮，亦皆陳於殿庭。

translations.literal: The Great Yellow Dragon Bearing the Chart Banner was displayed before the Gate of Illustrious Virtue; the remaining twenty banners were all set up before the lodging palace. When there were court assemblies or investiture ceremonies, they were also all displayed in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yellow Dragon Bearing the Chart banner was set before the Gate of Illustrious Virtue; the other twenty stood before the lodging palace. At court assemblies and investiture ceremonies, all were displayed in the palace courtyard as well.

sentences.zh: 凡馬步儀仗，共一萬一千二百二十二人，悉用禁軍。

translations.literal: In all, the mounted and foot ceremonial arms numbered 11,222 men, all drawn from the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: The mounted and foot ceremonial escort totaled 11,222 men, all drawn from the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、將軍以軍主、都虞候攝事，中郎將、都尉以指揮使、副指揮使攝事，校尉、主帥以軍使、副兵馬使、都頭、副都頭、十將攝事。

translations.literal: Grand generals and generals were represented by army commanders and chief adjutants; middle-ranking generals and commandants by regimental commanders and deputy regimental commanders; and company commanders and squad leaders by army inspectors, deputy cavalry inspectors, squad chiefs, deputy squad chiefs, and decurions.
translations.idiomatic: The ranks of grand general and general were filled by army commanders and chief adjutants; middle-ranking general and commandant by regimental commanders and their deputies; and company commander and squad leader by army inspectors, deputy cavalry inspectors, squad chiefs, deputy squad chiefs, and decurions.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，蜀平，命左拾遺孫逢吉收蜀法物，其不中度者悉毀之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, when Shu was pacified, the Left Reminder Sun Fengji was ordered to collect the ritual objects of Shu; those not conforming to standard were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande (965), after the conquest of Shu, the court ordered Left Reminder Sun Fengji to collect Shu's ritual objects and destroy any that failed to meet standard.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太祖親閱鹵簿。

translations.literal: That year, Emperor Taizu personally reviewed the procession insignia.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Emperor Taizu personally inspected the procession insignia.

sentences.zh: 四年，始令改畫衣為繡衣，至開寶三年而成，謂之「繡衣鹵簿」。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an order was first issued to change painted garments to embroidered garments. By the third year of Kaibao they were completed, and this was called the "Embroidered-Garment Procession Insignia."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande, the court ordered painted garments replaced with embroidered ones. The work was finished by the third year of Kaibao (970) and became known as the "Embroidered-Garment Procession."

sentences.zh: 其後郊祀皆用之。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was used for all suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it was used at every suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 軍衛羽儀，自是浸甚。

translations.literal: The military guards and feathered insignia from this time grew ever more elaborate.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, the military guards and feathered insignia grew steadily more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 每大祀，命大禮、禮儀、儀仗、鹵簿、橋道頓遞五使，鹵簿使專掌定字圖排列，儀仗使糾督之，大禮及餘使同按閱，致齋日巡仗。

translations.literal: For each great sacrifice, five commissioners were appointed—for Grand Ceremony, Rites, Ceremonial Arms, Procession Insignia, and Bridge-Road Relay Stations. The Procession Insignia Commissioner was solely responsible for fixing the character-diagram arrangements; the Ceremonial Arms Commissioner supervised them; the Grand Ceremony Commissioner and the others jointly inspected them; and on the day of abstention they patrolled the arms escort.
translations.idiomatic: For every great sacrifice, five commissioners were appointed—for Grand Ceremony, Rites, Ceremonial Arms, Procession Insignia, and Bridge-Road Relay Stations. The Procession Insignia Commissioner fixed the diagram arrangements, the Ceremonial Arms Commissioner supervised execution, the Grand Ceremony Commissioner and the others jointly inspected the formation, and on the abstention day they patrolled the escort.

sentences.zh: 又命殿前大校管勾捧日、奉宸隊，侍衛大校勾當儀仗兵隊，捧日、天武廂主四人，編排捧日、奉宸隊及執仗人，內諸司使、副使三員同押儀仗，別二員編排導引官。

translations.literal: Orders were also issued for a senior sergeant of the Palace Front to manage the Sun-Bearing and Imperial Service detachments, and a senior sergeant of the Imperial Guard to manage the ceremonial arms troops. Four squad chiefs of the Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial sections arranged the Sun-Bearing and Imperial Service detachments and the arms-bearers. Three commissioners and deputy commissioners of the inner bureaus jointly supervised the ceremonial arms, and two others separately arranged the guide officials.
translations.idiomatic: A senior sergeant of the Palace Front was put in charge of the Sun-Bearing and Imperial Service detachments, and a senior sergeant of the Imperial Guard of the ceremonial arms troops. Four squad chiefs of the Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial sections arranged those detachments and the arms-bearers. Three inner-bureau commissioners and deputies jointly supervised the ceremonial arms, while two others arranged the guide officials.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔節度使已下，除在京巡檢及押儀仗外，並令服褲褶衣導引。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict directed that military governors and all ranks below them, except those on capital patrol duty and those supervising ceremonial arms, were all to wear trousers and short jackets when serving as guides.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict required military governors and all ranks below them—except those on capital patrol or supervising ceremonial arms—to wear trousers and short jackets when serving as procession guides.

sentences.zh: 太宗至道中，令有司以絹畫為圖，圖凡三幅，中幅車輅、六引及導駕官，外兩幅儀衛，其警場青城，又別為圖，圖成，以藏秘閣。

translations.literal: In the Zhidao era under Emperor Taizong, the relevant offices were ordered to paint diagrams on silk. There were three scrolls in all: the center scroll showed the chariots, the six sections, and the officials guiding the imperial carriage; the two outer scrolls showed the ceremonial guards. The warning ground and the Green City were made into a separate diagram. When the diagrams were completed, they were stored in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Taizong's Zhidao era (995–997), the relevant offices were ordered to paint diagrams on silk—three scrolls in all, with chariots, the six sections, and guide officials on the center scroll and ceremonial guards on the outer two. The warning ground and Green City received a separate diagram. When finished, all were deposited in the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 凡仗內自行事官、排列職掌並捧日、奉宸、散手天武外，步騎一萬九千一百九十八人，此極盛也。

translations.literal: Within the arms escort, apart from the acting officials, those arranging duties, and the Sun-Bearing, Imperial Service, and Unattached Heavenly Martial detachments, the foot and mounted forces numbered 19,198 men—this was the greatest extent.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the acting officials, duty arrangers, and the Sun-Bearing, Imperial Service, and Unattached Heavenly Martial detachments, the foot and mounted forces within the escort reached 19,198 men—the high-water mark.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平五年，詔南郊儀仗引駕官，不得多帶從人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping under Emperor Zhenzong, an edict directed that officials leading the imperial carriage in the southern suburb ceremonial arms might not bring many attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianping (1002), Emperor Zhenzong decreed that officials escorting the imperial carriage in the southern suburb procession could not bring large retinues.

sentences.zh: 宰臣，親王，樞密、宣徽使，參知政事，樞密副使，三司使，各四人。

translations.literal: Chancellors, imperial princes, commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs and of the Palace Secretariat, vice grand councilors, vice commissioners of military affairs, and commissioners of the three fiscal departments—each four attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors, imperial princes, commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs and of the Palace Secretariat, vice grand councilors, vice commissioners of military affairs, and commissioners of the three fiscal departments were each limited to four attendants.

sentences.zh: 尚書，節度使，翰林學士、侍讀、侍講學士，各三人。

translations.literal: Ministers, military governors, Hanlin academicians, and lecturers-in-attendance and lecturers-in-waiting—each three attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, military governors, and Hanlin academicians, reading and lecturing attendants—each three attendants.

sentences.zh: 給事，諫議，知制誥，大卿監，金吾大將軍，樞密都承旨、副承旨，客省閣門使、副使，諸司使、副使至內殿崇班，各二人。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries, remonstrance officials, drafters of edicts, grand directors of bureaus, grand generals of the Golden Guard, chief and deputy receivers of the Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioners and deputy commissioners of the Reception and Gate offices, and bureau commissioners and deputies down to the Inner Hall Honored Class—each two attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries, remonstrance officials, edict drafters, grand bureau directors, Golden Guard grand generals, chief and deputy military-affairs receivers, reception and gate commissioners and deputies, and bureau commissioners down to the Inner Hall Honored Class—each two attendants.

sentences.zh: 少卿監，諸行郎中已下，閣門祗候已下，各一人。

translations.literal: Junior directors of bureaus, bureau section chiefs and below, and gate ushers and below—each one attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Junior bureau directors, section chiefs and below, and gate ushers and below—each one attendant.

sentences.zh: 又詔南郊引駕官，中書、樞密院一行在東，親王一行在西，餘依官次。

translations.literal: It was further decreed that among the officials leading the imperial carriage at the southern suburb, the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs formed one row on the east, imperial princes one row on the west, and the rest according to official rank.
translations.idiomatic: A further decree placed the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs in the eastern row, imperial princes in the western row, and all others according to rank.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，改小駕為鸞駕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the lesser imperial carriage was renamed the Luan Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008), the lesser imperial carriage was renamed the Luan Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 自太祖易繡衣鹵簿後，太宗、真宗皆增益之。

translations.literal: After Emperor Taizu changed to the embroidered-garment procession insignia, Emperors Taizong and Zhenzong both added to it.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizu introduced the embroidered-garment procession, both Taizong and Zhenzong enlarged it further.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，儀典多襲前世，宋綬定鹵簿，為《圖記》十卷上之，詔以付秘閣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, ceremonial regulations largely followed previous reigns. Song Shou fixed the procession insignia and presented a ten-scroll Illustrated Record; an edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Repository.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, ceremonial practice largely followed earlier reigns. Song Shou codified the procession insignia and presented a ten-scroll Illustrated Record, which the court ordered deposited in the Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 凡大駕，用二萬六十一人，大率以太僕寺主車輅，殿中省主輿輦、傘扇、御馬，金吾主纛、槊、十六騎、引駕細仗、牙門，六軍主槍仗，尚書兵部主六引諸隊、大角、五牛旗，門下省主寶案，司天台主鍾漏，太常主鼓吹，朝服法物庫出旗器、名物、衣冠、幰蓋，軍器庫出箙、弩、矢，內弓箭庫出戎裝、雜仗。

translations.literal: For the great imperial carriage in all, 20,061 men were used. In general the Court of the Imperial Stud managed the chariots; the Palace Department managed palanquins, umbrellas, fans, and imperial horses; the Golden Guard managed banners, spears, the sixteen riders, the fine arms of the imperial escort, and the gate guards; the Six Armies managed lances and arms; the Ministry of War in the Secretariat managed the six sections and their detachments, the great horn, and the five-ox banners; the Chancellery managed the imperial treasure table; the Directorate of Astronomy managed bells and clepsydrae; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices managed wind and percussion music; the Court Robes and Ritual Objects Storehouse issued banners, vessels, named objects, robes and caps, and carriage canopies; the Armory issued quivers, crossbows, and arrows; and the Inner Archery Storehouse issued military dress and miscellaneous arms.
translations.idiomatic: The great imperial procession employed 20,061 men in all. Broadly speaking, the Court of the Imperial Stud managed chariots; the Palace Department palanquins, umbrellas, fans, and imperial horses; the Golden Guard banners, spears, the sixteen riders, the fine escort arms, and gate guards; the Six Armies lances and arms; the Ministry of War the six sections and their detachments, the great horn, and five-ox banners; the Chancellery the imperial treasure table; the Directorate of Astronomy bells and clepsydrae; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices wind and percussion; the Court Robes and Ritual Objects Storehouse flags, vessels, regalia, and carriage canopies; the Armory quivers, crossbows, and arrows; and the Inner Archery Storehouse military dress and miscellaneous arms.

sentences.zh: 凡六引導駕、太僕卿、千牛將軍、殿中侍御史、司天監少府監僚佐局官、乘黃令、大將軍、金吾上將軍、將軍、六統軍，皆以京朝官內諸司使、副使以下攝事。

translations.literal: In all, the six sections guiding the imperial carriage, the director of the Imperial Stud, the thousand-ox general, the palace censor, the assistant officials of the Directorate of Astronomy and Court of the Imperial Workshops, the director of the Imperial Stables, grand generals, Golden Guard senior generals and generals, and the six army commanders—all were represented by capital officials, commissioners and deputy commissioners of the inner bureaus and below.
translations.idiomatic: The six escort sections, the director of the Imperial Stud, the thousand-ox general, the palace censor, assistant officials of the Directorate of Astronomy and Court of the Imperial Workshops, the director of the Imperial Stables, grand generals, Golden Guard senior generals and generals, and the six army commanders were all represented by capital officials—inner-bureau commissioners and deputies and below.

sentences.zh: 仗內用禁軍諸班直：捧日、天武、拱聖、神勇、宣武、驍騎、武勝、寧朔、虎翼兵。

translations.literal: Within the arms escort were used the various direct companies of the palace guard: Sun-Bearing, Heavenly Martial, Bowing-to-Sageliness, Spirit-Brave, Proclaiming Martial, Valiant Cavalry, Martial Victory, Pacifying the North, and Tiger Wing troops.
translations.idiomatic: The escort drew on the palace guard's direct companies: Sun-Bearing, Heavenly Martial, Bowing-to-Sageliness, Spirit-Brave, Proclaiming Martial, Valiant Cavalry, Martial Victory, Pacifying the North, and Tiger Wing.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、將軍以軍主、都虞候攝。

translations.literal: Grand generals and generals were represented by army commanders and chief adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: Grand generals and generals were represented by army commanders and chief adjutants.

sentences.zh: 中郎將、郎將、都尉以指揮使、副指揮使攝。

translations.literal: Middle-ranking generals, commanders, and commandants were represented by regimental commanders and deputy regimental commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-ranking generals, commanders, and commandants were represented by regimental commanders and their deputies.

sentences.zh: 校尉、主帥、旅帥、隊正以軍使、副兵馬使、都頭、副都頭、十將攝。

translations.literal: Company commanders, squad leaders, company chiefs, and platoon chiefs were represented by army inspectors, deputy cavalry inspectors, squad chiefs, deputy squad chiefs, and decurions.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders, squad leaders, company chiefs, and platoon chiefs were represented by army inspectors, deputy cavalry inspectors, squad chiefs, deputy squad chiefs, and decurions.

sentences.zh: 餘法駕、鸞駕、黃麾仗，則遞減其數。

translations.literal: For the remaining statutory carriage, luan carriage, and yellow-banner arms escort, the numbers were reduced in turn.
translations.idiomatic: For the statutory carriage, luan carriage, and yellow-banner escort, the numbers were reduced proportionally.

sentences.zh: 景祐五年，賈昌朝言儀衛三事：

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingyou, Jia Changchao spoke on three matters concerning ceremonial guards:
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jingyou (1038), Jia Changchao raised three matters concerning ceremonial guards:

sentences.zh: 一曰南郊鹵簿，車駕出宮詣郊廟日，執球杖供奉官，於導駕官前分列迎引，至於齋宮。

translations.literal: First, concerning the southern suburb procession insignia: on the day the imperial carriage left the palace for the suburban temple, the tribute officials bearing ball-staves lined up in separate ranks before the officials guiding the carriage to welcome and lead it as far as the abstention palace.
translations.idiomatic: First, regarding the southern suburb procession: on the day the emperor left the palace for the suburban temple, tribute officials bearing ball-staves formed ranks ahead of the guide officials to welcome and escort the carriage as far as the abstention palace.

sentences.zh: 夫球杖非古，蓋唐世尚之，以資玩樂。

translations.literal: Ball-staves are not ancient; they were esteemed in the Tang dynasty for amusement and play.
translations.idiomatic: Ball-staves are not an ancient institution; the Tang court favored them for amusement.

sentences.zh: 其執之者皆褻服，錦繡珠玉，過於侈麗，既不足以昭文物，又不可以備軍容。

translations.literal: Those who bore them all wore informal dress, brocade, embroidery, pearls, and jade—excessively lavish. This was insufficient to display ritual objects, and could not serve as military bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Those who carried them wore informal dress adorned with brocade, embroidery, pearls, and jade—far too lavish to display ritual dignity and utterly unsuited to military bearing.

sentences.zh: 常時豫遊，或宜施用。

translations.literal: At ordinary times for preparatory excursions, their use might be appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: They might be appropriate for ordinary pleasure outings.

sentences.zh: 方今夙夜齋戒，親奉大祀，端冕顒昂，鼓吹不作，而乃陳戲賞之具，參簪紳之列，導迎法駕，入於祠宮。

translations.literal: But now, after days and nights of fasting and abstention, personally conducting the great sacrifice, wearing the correct cap and robes with solemn bearing, with wind and percussion silenced—yet playthings for amusement are displayed, mingling with the ranks of officials, guiding and welcoming the statutory carriage into the sacrificial palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, after days of fasting and abstention, as the emperor personally conducts the great sacrifice in full regalia with wind and percussion silenced, these playthings are displayed among the officials, escorting the statutory carriage into the sacrificial palace.

sentences.zh: 稽諸典儀，未為允稱。

translations.literal: Checked against canonical ritual, this is not acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against canonical ritual, this is hardly fitting.

sentences.zh: 況導駕官兩省員數悉備，何煩更有此色供奉官，謂宜徹去球杖，俟禮畢還宮，鼓吹振作，即復使就列。

translations.literal: Moreover, the guide officials of the two departments are fully staffed—why trouble to have these tribute officials of this sort? It is proposed that the ball-staves be removed; after the rites are completed and the emperor returns to the palace, when wind and percussion resume, they may take their places again.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, both departments already field a full complement of guide officials—why keep these tribute officials at all? He proposed removing the ball-staves during the rite and restoring them to formation only after the ceremony, when the emperor returned to the palace and wind and percussion resumed.

sentences.zh: 二曰大駕鹵簿，有羊車前列。

translations.literal: Second, in the great imperial procession insignia, there is a sheep carriage placed in the front ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the great imperial procession places a sheep carriage in the front ranks.

sentences.zh: 臣案羊車本漢、晉之代，乘於後宮。

translations.literal: Your subject finds that the sheep carriage originated in the Han and Jin dynasties and was ridden in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject notes that the sheep carriage originated in the Han and Jin eras as transport for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，增金寶之飾，駕以小駟，馭以丱童，自是以來，遂為法從。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, gold and treasure ornaments were added; it was drawn by small teams of four and driven by topknotted youths. From that time it became part of the statutory escort.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui in the Daye era, it was adorned with gold and jewels, drawn by small four-horse teams and driven by topknotted youths. Since then it has formed part of the statutory escort.

sentences.zh: 唐制兼有輦車、副車之名，國朝因循，尚未改革。

translations.literal: Tang regulations also had the names palanquin carriage and attendant carriage. Our dynasty has followed this and has not yet reformed it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang regulations also recognized palanquin and attendant carriages. Our dynasty has followed suit without reform.

sentences.zh: 竊以郊祭天地，廟見祖宗，車服所陳，動必由禮。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that in sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburb and appearing before the ancestors in the temple, whatever carriages and dress are displayed must at every point accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that in suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and temple appearances before the ancestors, every carriage and garment on display must conform to ritual.

sentences.zh: 至於四望、耕根之屬，兼包歷代，皆或有因，豈容後宮所乘，參陪五輅。

translations.literal: As for the Four Observations, Ploughing the Sacred Field, and the like, which embrace successive dynasties and all have some precedent—how can a vehicle ridden in the inner palace be allowed to join the five imperial chariots?
translations.idiomatic: Rites such as the Four Observations and Ploughing the Sacred Field draw on precedents from many dynasties—but how can a vehicle of the inner palace stand alongside the five imperial chariots?

sentences.zh: 欲望大駕不用羊車，所冀肅恭，稽合典禮。

translations.literal: Your subject desires that the great imperial carriage not use the sheep carriage, hoping thereby for solemn reverence in accord with canonical ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks that the great imperial procession dispense with the sheep carriage, so that solemnity may accord with canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 三曰南郊大駕鹵簿，儀衛甚眾，有司雖依典禮，名物次第，兵杖數目，預先分布，及五使量行案閱。

translations.literal: Third, concerning the southern suburb great imperial procession insignia: the ceremonial guards are very numerous. Although the relevant offices distribute in advance according to canonical ritual the named objects in sequence and the numbers of weapons and arms, and the five commissioners measure and inspect on the march—
translations.idiomatic: Third, the southern suburb great imperial procession fields a vast ceremonial guard. Although the relevant offices distribute named objects, weapon counts, and formation order in advance according to canonical ritual, and the five commissioners inspect on the march—

sentences.zh: 其如被差執掌吏員兵伍，素不閑習，行列先後，多失次序；

translations.literal: yet the clerks, soldiers, and troops assigned to take charge are by nature unpracticed, and the front and rear of the ranks often lose proper order;
translations.idiomatic: the clerks and soldiers assigned to take charge are by nature unpracticed, and ranks frequently fall out of order;

sentences.zh: 所持名物，亦或差互。

translations.literal: the named objects they hold are also sometimes confused.
translations.idiomatic: the named objects they carry are sometimes wrong as well.

sentences.zh: 押當官但以行事為名，從便趨進，失其處守。

translations.literal: The supervising officials act only in name for the occasion, advancing as convenient and losing their assigned positions.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising officials treat the duty as a formality, advancing as convenient and abandoning their assigned posts.

sentences.zh: 竊謂三載親郊，國之大事，旁陳象物，仰法乾行，四方之人，觀禮於是，宜詳制度，以示光華。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the triennial personal suburban sacrifice is a great affair of state. The ritual objects displayed on every side take Heaven's motion as their model; people from the four directions observe the ritual here. The regulations should be made detailed to display splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that the triennial personal suburban sacrifice is a great affair of state. Ritual objects displayed on every side model Heaven's motion, and observers from all directions watch here. The regulations ought to be made thorough enough to display the court's splendor.

sentences.zh: 請大駕鹵簿前後仗衛次第，於致齋前命儀仗、鹵簿使令有司執簿籍率押當官暨諸衛、諸省執仗士卒將領者，自殿門至郊廟分列之處，詳視先後及器仗名品，無令差忒。

translations.literal: It is requested that before the abstention day, the Ceremonial Arms and Procession Insignia commissioners order the relevant offices, ledgers in hand, to lead the supervising officials together with the guards and secretariat soldiers bearing arms and their commanders, from the palace gate to the suburban temple, to examine in detail at each place where ranks are formed the front and rear order and the names and grades of vessels and arms, so that there be no error.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that before the abstention day the Ceremonial Arms and Procession Insignia commissioners have the relevant offices lead supervising officials, guard and secretariat arms-bearers, and their commanders—with ledgers in hand—from the palace gate to the suburban temple, examining at each formation point the order of ranks and the names and grades of vessels and arms so that no error remained.

sentences.zh: 詔禮儀使宋綬與太常禮院同詳定以奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rites Commissioner Song Shou and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office jointly to work out the details and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Rites Commissioner Song Shou and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office to work out the details jointly and memorialize.

sentences.zh: 綬奏：「鹵簿內有諸司供奉，蓋資備物，以奉乘輿。

translations.literal: Shou memorialized: "Within the procession insignia there are tribute officials of the various bureaus, who supply prepared objects to serve the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shou memorialized: "The procession includes tribute officials from the various bureaus who supply prepared objects for the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 今昌朝言宿齋之時，不可陳玩樂之具。

translations.literal: Now Changchao says that during the overnight abstention, playthings for amusement must not be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Changchao now argues that during the overnight abstention, playthings must not be displayed.

sentences.zh: 請郊祀前一日，應供奉官等令宿幕次，俟皇帝行禮畢降壇，導至青城，由青城前導歸大內。

translations.literal: It is requested that on the day before the suburban sacrifice, the tribute officials and others be ordered to lodge in the tent quarters, and after the emperor completes the rites and descends the altar, to guide him to the Green City, and from before the Green City guide his return to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that on the eve of the suburban sacrifice the tribute officials lodge in the tent quarters, then after the emperor completed the rites and descended the altar, guide him to the Green City and from there back to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後漢劉熙《釋名》曰：「騾車、羊車，各以所駕名之也。」

translations.literal: Liu Xi of Later Han in Explanation of Names says: "The mule carriage and sheep carriage are each named for what draws them."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi of Later Han writes in Explanation of Names: "The mule carriage and sheep carriage are each named for their draft animals."

sentences.zh: 隋《禮儀志》曰：「漢氏或以人牽，或駕果下馬。」

translations.literal: The Sui Treatise on Ritual says: "Under the Han dynasty it was sometimes drawn by men, sometimes drawn by pony horses."
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise on Ritual records: "Under the Han it was sometimes drawn by men, sometimes by pony horses."

sentences.zh: 此乃漢代已有，晉武偶取乘於後宮，非特為掖庭製也。

translations.literal: This shows it already existed in the Han dynasty; Jin Emperor Wu happened to take it for riding in the inner palace—it was not made specially for the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the carriage existed in Han times; Jin Emperor Wu happened to use it in the inner palace—it was not made solely for the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 況歷代載於《輿服志》，自唐至今，著之禮令，宜且仍舊。

translations.literal: Moreover, successive dynasties record it in the Treatise on Carriages and Dress; from Tang to the present it is set down in ritual statutes. It is appropriate for the time being to keep the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, successive dynasties recorded it in the Treatise on Carriages and Dress, and from Tang to the present it has stood in ritual statutes. For now it should remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其鹵簿儀仗，遇南郊前，五使預閱素備，願依昌朝所奏，下儀仗、鹵簿使加點閱，使之齊肅。」

translations.literal: As for the procession insignia and ceremonial arms, before the southern suburb the five commissioners' preliminary inspection is always in place. It is wished that, in accordance with what Changchao memorialized, the Ceremonial Arms and Procession Insignia commissioners be ordered to add inspection points so that they may be orderly and solemn."
translations.idiomatic: As for the procession insignia and ceremonial arms, the five commissioners' preliminary inspection before the southern suburb is already established. He asked that, following Changchao's proposal, the Ceremonial Arms and Procession Insignia commissioners add inspection points to ensure order and solemnity."

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，將享明堂，鹵簿使奏：「法駕減大駕三分之一，而兵部亡字圖故本，且文牘散逸，雖粗有名數，較之禮令，未有以裁其中。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou, when the Bright Hall was to be enjoyed, the Procession Insignia Commissioner memorialized: "The statutory carriage reduces the great imperial carriage by one third, but the Ministry of War has lost the old character-diagram manuscript, and documents are scattered and lost. Although there are rough name counts, compared with the ritual statutes there is no means to determine what lies between."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangyou (1050), as the court prepared to worship at the Bright Hall, the Procession Insignia Commissioner reported: "The statutory carriage reduces the great imperial procession by one third, but the Ministry of War has lost the old character-diagram manuscript and many documents have been scattered. Although rough head counts exist, they cannot be reconciled with the ritual statutes."

sentences.zh: 詔禮官與兵部加考正，為圖以奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ritual officials and the Ministry of War to add examination and correction and present a diagram.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered ritual officials and the Ministry of War to verify and correct the records and present a diagram.

sentences.zh: 及上圖，法駕鹵簿用萬有一千八十八人。

translations.literal: When the diagram was submitted, the statutory carriage procession insignia used 10,088 men.
translations.idiomatic: When the diagram was submitted, the statutory carriage procession employed 10,088 men.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年祫享，用禮儀使奏：「南郊仗，金吾上將軍、六統軍、左右千牛，皆服紫繡戎服，珂珮，騎而前；

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, at the collective offering, the Rites Commissioner memorialized for use: "In the southern suburb arms escort, the Golden Guard senior generals, the six army commanders, and the Left and Right Thousand-Ox—all wear purple embroidered military dress with jade pendants, riding forward;
translations.idiomatic: At the collective offering in the second year of Jiayou (1057), the Rites Commissioner reported: "In the southern suburb escort, Golden Guard senior generals, the six army commanders, and the Left and Right Thousand-Ox all wear purple embroidered military dress with jade pendants, riding forward;

sentences.zh: 節度使亦衣褲褶導駕，如舊例。」

translations.literal: military governors also wear trousers and short jackets to guide the imperial carriage, as in the old precedent."
translations.idiomatic: military governors also wear trousers and short jackets to guide the carriage, as before."

sentences.zh: 是月，禮官奏：「南郊還，在禮當乘金輅，而或詔乘大輦，宜著於令，常以大輦從。」

translations.literal: That month, the ritual officials memorialized: "On return from the southern suburb, according to ritual one should ride the golden chariot, but sometimes an edict orders riding the great palanquin. This should be set down in the statutes: ordinarily follow with the great palanquin."
translations.idiomatic: That month ritual officials reported: "On return from the southern suburb, ritual prescribes the golden chariot, yet edicts sometimes order the great palanquin instead. This should be written into statute: the great palanquin should normally follow."

sentences.zh: 六年，幸睦親宅，內侍抱駕頭墮馬，駕頭壞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when visiting the Mansion of Cordial Kinship, an inner attendant holding the carriage head fell from his horse and the carriage head was damaged.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, during a visit to the Mansion of Cordial Kinship, an inner attendant holding the carriage head fell from his horse and the carriage head was broken.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞韓絳奏請嚴儀衛，事下閣門、太常禮院議。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Han Jiang memorialized requesting stricter ceremonial guards. The matter was sent down to the Gate Office and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Han Jiang memorialized for stricter ceremonial guards. The matter was referred to the Gate Office and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Office.

sentences.zh: 遂合奏：「車駕出，請以閣門祗候及內侍各二員，扶駕頭左右，次扇筤，又以皇城親從兵二十人從其後。」

translations.literal: They jointly memorialized: "When the imperial carriage goes out, let two gate ushers and two inner attendants support the carriage head on left and right, then the fan rack, and let twenty personal followers from the Imperial City guard follow behind."
translations.idiomatic: They jointly proposed: "When the imperial carriage goes out, two gate ushers and two inner attendants should support the carriage head on either side, followed by the fan rack, with twenty Imperial City personal guards behind."

sentences.zh: 神宗熙寧七年，詔太常看詳兵部大駕鹵簿字圖，遂奏言：「製器尚象，有其數者，必有其義。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xining under Emperor Shenzong, an edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine in detail the Ministry of War's character diagram for the great imperial procession insignia. They memorialized: "In making vessels one values images; where there are numbers, there must be meanings.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xining (1074), Emperor Shenzong ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to review the Ministry of War's character diagram for the great imperial procession. They reported: "In making ritual vessels one values symbolic forms; where there are numbers, there must be meaning.

sentences.zh: 後世車駕儀仗，多雜秦、漢制度，當革其尤者。

translations.literal: The carriages and ceremonial arms of later ages mix in many Qin and Han institutions; the most egregious should be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Later imperial carriages and ceremonial arms mix in many Qin and Han practices; the worst excesses should be reformed.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·車仆》：「凡師，共革車，各以其萃。」

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, Master of Chariots: "Whenever the army marches, supply leather chariots, each with its attendant chariot."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Master of Chariots, states: "Whenever the army marches, supply leather chariots, each with its attendant chariot."

sentences.zh: 萃，副車也。

translations.literal: Cui means attendant chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Cui means attendant chariot.

sentences.zh: 諸輅之副，宜次正輅。

translations.literal: The attendant chariots of the various imperial chariots should follow immediately after the main chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant chariots for each imperial chariot should follow immediately behind the main chariot.

sentences.zh: 羊車，前代宮中所乘；

translations.literal: The sheep carriage was ridden in the inner palace in former ages;
translations.idiomatic: The sheep carriage was used in the inner palace in earlier ages;

sentences.zh: 五牛旗，蓋古之五時副車也，以木牛載旗，用人輿之，失其本製：宜除去。」

translations.literal: the five-ox banner was probably the five-season attendant chariot of antiquity. Using a wooden ox to carry a banner and having men shoulder it loses the original design: both should be removed."
translations.idiomatic: the five-ox banner was probably the five-season attendant chariot of antiquity. Carrying a banner on a wooden ox borne by men departs from the original design: both should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 又禮文所言：

translations.literal: Further, on what the ritual texts say:
translations.idiomatic: The ritual texts further state:

sentences.zh: 近製，金輅不以金飾諸末，象輅不以象飾諸末，革輅不鞔，木輅不漆，請改飾四輅。

translations.literal: In recent manufacture, the golden chariot is not adorned with gold at its extremities, the elephant chariot is not adorned with elephant at its extremities, the leather chariot is not covered with leather, and the wooden chariot is not lacquered. It is requested that the four chariots be re-adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent practice the golden chariot lacks gold ornament at its extremities, the elephant chariot lacks ivory ornament, the leather chariot is not covered in leather, and the wooden chariot is not lacquered. They asked that all four chariots be properly adorned.

sentences.zh: 太常則繪三辰，加升龍、降龍，大旂則繪交龍、大赤鳥隼、大白熊虎、大麾龜蛇而去其雲龍，使之應禮。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices banner should be painted with the three luminaries, with ascending and descending dragons added. The great banner should be painted with intertwined dragons; the great red with birds of prey; the great white with bears and tigers; the great black-standard with tortoise and serpent—and the cloud-dragon removed—so that they accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices banner should bear the three luminaries with ascending and descending dragons. The great banner should show intertwined dragons; the great red banner birds of prey; the great white bears and tigers; the great black-standard tortoise and serpent—with cloud-dragons removed—so that all accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 又古者，五輅皆載旗，謂之「道德之車。」

translations.literal: Moreover, in antiquity all five chariots bore banners and were called "chariots of moral power."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity all five chariots bore banners and were called "chariots of moral power."

sentences.zh: 《考工記》車戟崇於殳，酋矛崇於戟，各四赤，戟矛皆插車騎，謂之「兵車」。

translations.literal: The Record of Crafts says: chariot halberds are set higher than shu polearms, and chieftain spears higher than halberds—each four chi—and halberds and spears are all planted on the chariot flanks; these are called "military chariots."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Crafts specifies that chariot halberds stand higher than shu polearms and chieftain spears higher than halberds—each four chi—with halberds and spears planted on the chariot flanks; these are called "military chariots."

sentences.zh: 戰國尚武，故增插四戟，謂之闟戟」。

translations.literal: The Warring States prized martial affairs, so four additional halberds were planted, called "closing halberds."
translations.idiomatic: The Warring States prized martial display, so four additional halberds were added—called "closing halberds."

sentences.zh: 則知德車、武車，固異用矣。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that moral chariots and military chariots were originally for different uses.
translations.idiomatic: Thus moral chariots and military chariots served distinct purposes from the outset.

sentences.zh: 漢鹵簿，前驅有鳳凰闟戟，猶未施於五輅。

translations.literal: In the Han procession insignia, the vanguard had phoenix closing-halberds, but they were not yet applied to the five chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Han procession insignia placed phoenix closing-halberds in the vanguard but did not yet mount them on the five chariots.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，五輅乃加棨戟於車之右，韜以黼繡之衣。

translations.literal: From the Eastern Jin onward, the five chariots added halberd-poles on the right side of the chariot, sheathed in brocade-embroidered covers.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Jin onward, the five chariots bore halberd-poles on the right side, sheathed in brocade-embroidered covers.

sentences.zh: 後周司輅，左建旗，右建闟戟，闟戟方六尺，而被之以黼，皆戾於古。

translations.literal: Under Later Zhou the Master of Chariots set up a banner on the left and closing-halberds on the right; the closing-halberds were six chi square and covered with fu-pattern brocade—all contrary to antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou the Master of Chariots placed a banner on the left and closing-halberds on the right—six chi square and covered in fu-pattern brocade—all departing from ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 請去五輅闟戟，以應「 道德」之稱，而建太常於車後之中央，升輅則由左。

translations.literal: It is requested that the closing-halberds on the five chariots be removed, to accord with the title "moral power," and that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices banner be set at the center rear of the chariot; when mounting the chariot, one ascends from the left.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that closing-halberds be removed from the five chariots to match the title "chariots of moral power," that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices banner be mounted at the center rear of each chariot, and that one mount from the left.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮》：「大馭，掌馭玉輅以祀。」

translations.literal: Further, according to the Rites of Zhou: "The Grand Charioteer manages driving the jade chariot for sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: They further cited the Rites of Zhou: "The Grand Charioteer drives the jade chariot for sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 則祀乘玉輅也。

translations.literal: Thus for sacrifice one rides the jade chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one rides the jade chariot for the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 齋仆掌馭金輅，齋右充金輅之右，則齋乘金輅也。

translations.literal: The Abstention Charioteer manages driving the golden chariot; the Abstention Right fills the right of the golden chariot—thus for abstention one rides the golden chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Abstention Charioteer drives the golden chariot, and the Abstention Right occupies its right side—thus one rides the golden chariot during abstention.

sentences.zh: 齋祀之車，異用而不相因。

translations.literal: The chariots for abstention and sacrifice are for different uses and do not follow upon one another.
translations.idiomatic: The chariots for abstention and sacrifice serve different purposes and should not be conflated.

sentences.zh: 國朝親祠太廟，致齋文德殿，翌日即進玉輅，非製。

translations.literal: In our dynasty, when personally sacrificing at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, abstention is held in the Hall of Literary Virtue, and the next day the jade chariot is advanced immediately—not according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty the emperor personally sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple after abstaining in the Hall of Literary Virtue, then advances the jade chariot the very next day—contrary to regulation.

sentences.zh: 請進金輅，俟太廟祠畢，翌日，禦玉輅詣郊。

translations.literal: It is requested that the golden chariot be advanced; after the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifice is completed, on the following day ride the jade chariot to the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the golden chariot be advanced first and that, after the ancestral temple rites, the emperor ride the jade chariot to the suburb on the following day.

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》戎右職曰：「會同，充革車。」

translations.literal: Further, the Rites of Zhou duty of the Military Right says: "At the assembly of the feudal lords, fill the leather chariot."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also assigns the Military Right: "At the assembly of feudal lords, occupy the leather chariot."

sentences.zh: 《儀禮》曰：「貳車畢乘。」

translations.literal: The Ceremonies and Rites says: "The secondary chariot is fully occupied."
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonies and Rites states: "The secondary chariot must be fully occupied."

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰：「乘君之乘車，不敢曠左，左必式。」

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: "When riding the ruler's carriage, one dare not leave the left seat empty; on the left one must bow with hands on the crossbar."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites adds: "When riding the ruler's carriage, one must not leave the left seat vacant; whoever occupies the left must bow with hands on the crossbar."

sentences.zh: 蓋古者後車餘輅，不敢曠空，必使人乘之，所以別曠左之嫌也。

translations.literal: For in antiquity the rear chariots and surplus chariots dared not be left empty; people had to ride in them—this was to avoid the suspicion of leaving the left seat vacant.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity rear and surplus chariots could not be left empty; someone had to ride in each, precisely to avoid the impropriety of a vacant left seat.

sentences.zh: 自秦兼九國車服，西漢因之，大駕屬車八十一乘。

translations.literal: From the time Qin annexed the nine states' carriages and dress, Western Han followed this; the great imperial carriage had eighty-one attendant chariots.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin absorbed the nine states' carriage regalia, Western Han followed suit, assigning eighty-one attendant chariots to the great imperial train.

sentences.zh: 《後漢志》云：「尚書、御史所載。」

translations.literal: The Treatise of Later Han says: "Carried by the Secretariat and the Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise of Later Han records: "Carried by the Secretariat and the Censorate."

sentences.zh: 揚雄曰：「鴟夷國器，托於屬車。」

translations.literal: Yang Xiong said: "The owl-vessel, a vessel of state, was entrusted to the attendant chariots."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong wrote: "The owl-vessel, a vessel of state, was entrusted to the attendant chariots."

sentences.zh: 則是漢之屬車，非獨載人，又以載物，亦《儀禮》所謂「畢乘」之義也。

translations.literal: Thus the attendant chariots of Han did not only carry people but also carried objects—this too is the meaning of "fully occupied" in the Ceremonies and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Han attendant chariots carried not only passengers but also goods—the very sense of "fully occupied" in the Ceremonies and Rites.

sentences.zh: 國朝鹵簿，車十二乘，虛設於法駕之後，實近曠左之嫌。

translations.literal: In our dynasty's procession insignia, twelve chariots are set up empty behind the statutory carriage—this in fact comes close to the impropriety of leaving the left seat vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's procession places twelve empty chariots behind the statutory carriage—nearly the impropriety of a vacant left seat.

sentences.zh: 請令尚書、御史乘之，或以載乘輿服御。

translations.literal: It is requested that the Secretariat and Censorate ride in them, or that they be used to carry the imperial carriage's dress and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the Secretariat and Censorate ride in them, or that the chariots carry the emperor's dress and regalia.

sentences.zh: 又言：「法駕之行，必有共輿者，蓋以承清問。

translations.literal: It was further said: "When the statutory carriage travels, there must be one who shares the carriage, to receive the ruler's inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: They further argued: "When the statutory carriage travels, someone must share the ride to receive the ruler's inquiries.

sentences.zh: 《周官》有太僕、齋仆、道仆，所以御車，至參乘，則其禮益重。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou have the Grand Charioteer, Abstention Charioteer, and Procession Charioteer to drive the chariot; as for the co-rider, that ritual is still more weighty.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou appoint a Grand Charioteer, Abstention Charioteer, and Procession Charioteer to drive the chariot; the co-rider's role is still more exalted.

sentences.zh: 故道德之車則有齋右、道右，武車則有戎右，皆以士大夫為之。

translations.literal: Thus moral chariots have the Abstention Right and Procession Right; military chariots have the Military Right—all filled by scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Moral chariots therefore have an Abstention Right and Procession Right; military chariots a Military Right—all held by scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 國朝之制，乘輿有太僕而無參乘，請增近臣一員，立車右。」

translations.literal: In our dynasty's regulations, the imperial carriage has a Grand Charioteer but no co-rider. It is requested that one close minister be added to stand as Chariot Right."
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty provides a Grand Charioteer but no co-rider for the imperial carriage. They asked that one close minister be added as Chariot Right."

sentences.zh: 其後，詔增製五輅及參乘，玉輅建太常，金輅建大旂，象輅建大赤，革輅建大白，木輅建大麾。

translations.literal: Thereafter, an edict ordered additional manufacture of the five chariots and co-riders. The jade chariot bore the Court of Imperial Sacrifices banner; the golden chariot the great banner; the elephant chariot the great red; the leather chariot the great white; the wooden chariot the great black-standard.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter an edict ordered new five chariots and co-riders: the jade chariot bore the Court of Imperial Sacrifices banner, the golden the great banner, the elephant the great red, the leather the great white, and the wooden the great black-standard.

sentences.zh: 諸輅之副，各次正輅，仍存闟戟焉。

translations.literal: The attendant chariots of the various chariots each followed the main chariot; closing-halberds were still retained.
translations.idiomatic: Each chariot's attendants followed immediately behind, though closing-halberds were retained.

sentences.zh: 時大駕鹵簿，仗下官一百四十六員，執仗、押引從軍員、職掌諸軍諸司二萬二千二百二十一人。

translations.literal: At that time the great imperial procession insignia had 146 officials under the arms escort, and 22,221 soldiers bearing arms, supervising and guiding, and staff of the various armies and bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the great imperial procession fielded 146 officials under the arms escort and 22,221 soldiers bearing arms, supervising guides, and staff from the various armies and bureaus.

sentences.zh: 初，玉輅自唐顯慶中傳之，號「顯慶輅」。

translations.literal: Initially, the jade chariot had been handed down from the Xianqing era of Tang and was called the "Xianqing Chariot."
translations.idiomatic: The jade chariot had been handed down from the Tang Xianqing era and was known as the "Xianqing Chariot."

sentences.zh: 神宗更製新玉輅，六年正月，禦大慶殿受朝，先夕陳諸庭，夜半徹幕屋，壓焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong had a new jade chariot made. In the first month of the sixth year, when holding court in the Hall of Great Celebration, it was displayed in the courtyard the evening before; at midnight the tent shelter was removed and it was crushed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong ordered a new jade chariot built. On the eve of receiving court in the Hall of Great Celebration in the first month of the sixth year, it was displayed in the courtyard; at midnight workers removed the sheltering tent and the chariot was crushed.

sentences.zh: 自是竟乘舊輅。

translations.literal: From then on he always rode the old chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he always rode the old chariot.

sentences.zh: 高宗初至南京，孟太后以乘輿服御及禦輦儀仗來進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong first arrived at Nanjing, Empress Dowager Meng presented the imperial carriage's dress and regalia together with the imperial palanquin's ceremonial arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong first reached Nanjing, Empress Dowager Meng presented the imperial carriage's dress and regalia along with the imperial palanquin's ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，詔東京所屬起發祭器、法服、儀仗赴行在所。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era, an edict ordered the authorities of the Eastern Capital to dispatch ritual vessels, statutory dress, and ceremonial arms to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era, an edict ordered the Eastern Capital authorities to send ritual vessels, statutory dress, and ceremonial arms to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 十一月，帝郊於揚州，儀仗用一千三百五十五人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the emperor sacrificed at the suburb in Yangzhou; the ceremonial arms used 1,355 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor performed a suburban sacrifice at Yangzhou with a ceremonial escort of 1,355 men.

sentences.zh: 倉卒渡江，皆為金兵所焚。

translations.literal: In the hasty crossing of the river, all were burned by the Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the hasty flight south across the river, Jin troops burned them all.

sentences.zh: 紹興十二年，有司言：「天子起居，當備法駕，況太母回鑾，將奉郊迎。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing, the relevant offices said: "For the Son of Heaven's daily movements, the statutory carriage should be prepared; moreover, the Grand Empress Dowager is returning to the capital and a suburban welcome will be offered."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Shaoxing (1142), the relevant offices reported: "The Son of Heaven's daily movements require a statutory carriage; moreover, the Grand Empress Dowager is returning to the capital and will be welcomed with a suburban ceremony."

sentences.zh: 遂令工部尚書莫將等檢會本朝文德、大慶殿舊儀，下太常定，用二千二百六十五人，於是始備黃麾仗，慶、冊、親饗皆用焉。

translations.literal: They were ordered to have Minister of Works Mo Jiang and others check the old rites of the Hall of Literary Virtue and Hall of Great Celebration of this dynasty and send them down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for fixing, using 2,265 men. Thereupon the yellow-banner arms escort was first prepared; celebrations, investitures, and personal offerings all used it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Minister of Works Mo Jiang and others to collate the old rites of the Halls of Literary Virtue and Great Celebration and refer them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, fixing the escort at 2,265 men. The yellow-banner arms escort was thus first established and used for celebrations, investitures, and personal offerings.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，玉輅成。

translations.literal: That winter, the jade chariot was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the jade chariot was completed.

sentences.zh: 明年，郊，準國初大駕之數，一萬一千二百二十二人。

translations.literal: The next year, at the suburban sacrifice, following the number of the great imperial carriage at the founding of the dynasty: 11,222 men.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, at the suburban sacrifice, the escort followed the founding-era great imperial count of 11,222 men.

sentences.zh: 內舊用錦襖子者以纈繒代，用銅革帶者以勒帛代。

translations.literal: Among them, where brocade jackets had been used, patterned silk was substituted; where copper leather belts had been used, woven belts were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade jackets were replaced with patterned silk, and copper leather belts with woven belts.

sentences.zh: 而指揮使、都頭仍舊用錦帽子、錦臂袖者，以方勝練鵲羅代；

translations.literal: Where regimental commanders and squad chiefs still used brocade caps and brocade arm-sleeves, square-motif silk with paired-magpie pattern was substituted;
translations.idiomatic: Regimental commanders and squad chiefs who still wore brocade caps and arm-sleeves received square-motif silk with paired-magpie pattern instead;

sentences.zh: 用絁者以綢代。

translations.literal: where ramie had been used, silk was substituted.
translations.idiomatic: ramie garments were replaced with silk.

sentences.zh: 禁衛班直服色，用錦繡、金銀、真珠、北珠者七百八十人，以頭帽、銀帶、纈羅衫代。

translations.literal: For the palace guard direct companies' dress colors, 780 men who had used brocade embroidery, gold and silver, true pearls, and northern pearls were given head caps, silver belts, and patterned silk robes instead.
translations.idiomatic: For 780 palace-guard direct companies who had worn brocade, gold and silver, and pearls, head caps, silver belts, and patterned silk robes were substituted.

sentences.zh: 旗物用繡者，以錯采代；

translations.literal: Where flags and objects used embroidery, mixed colors were substituted;
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered flags and objects were replaced with mixed-color versions;

sentences.zh: 車路院香鐙案、衣褥、睥睨，禦輦院華蓋、曲蓋及仗內幢角等袋用繡者，以生色代。

translations.literal: the incense-lamp tables, bedding, and parapets of the Chariot Road Office; the ornate canopies, curved canopies, and banner-corner bags within the escort that used embroidery from the Imperial Palanquin Office—all were replaced with plain-dyed goods.
translations.idiomatic: embroidered items from the Chariot Road and Imperial Palanquin offices—including incense-lamp tables, bedding, parapets, canopies, and banner-corner bags—were replaced with plain-dyed goods.

sentences.zh: 殿前司仗內金槍、銀槍、旗幹，易以漆飾；

translations.literal: The golden spears, silver spears, and flagpoles within the escort of the Palace Front Office were changed to lacquer ornament;
translations.idiomatic: Golden and silver spears and flagpoles in the Palace Front escort were given lacquer ornament instead;

sentences.zh: 而拂扇、坐褥以珠飾者去之。

translations.literal: and pearl ornament on whisk-fans and seat cushions was removed.
translations.idiomatic: pearl ornament on whisk-fans and seat cushions was removed.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「事天貴質，若惟事華麗，非初意矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In serving Heaven, simplicity is valued. If one attends only to splendor, that is not the original intent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In serving Heaven, simplicity is paramount. To pursue splendor alone betrays our original intent."

sentences.zh: 十月，鹵簿器物及金象革木四輅、大安輦皆成。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the procession insignia vessels and the golden, elephant, leather, and wooden chariots and the Great Peace Palanquin were all completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the procession vessels and the golden, elephant, leather, and wooden chariots and the Great Peace Palanquin were all completed.

sentences.zh: 太常又奏，前後六引鼓吹八百八十四人，舊制騎。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices further memorialized that the wind and percussion of the front and rear six sections numbered 884 men; by old regulation they rode.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices further reported that the front and rear six sections' wind and percussion corps numbered 884 men and had ridden by old regulation.

sentences.zh: 今路狹擁遏，欲止令步導。

translations.literal: Now the road is narrow and congested; it is desired to stop this and order them to guide on foot only.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roads were narrow and congested, they asked that the musicians guide on foot only.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 十六年，始增捧日、奉宸隊，合一萬五千五十人。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Sun-Bearing and Imperial Service detachments were first increased, totaling 15,050 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the Sun-Bearing and Imperial Service detachments were first enlarged, bringing the total to 15,050 men.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿之制備矣。

translations.literal: The regulations for procession insignia were now complete.
translations.idiomatic: The procession regulations were now complete.

sentences.zh: 三十一年九月，行明堂禮，儀物視郊祀省三之一，用一萬一千五人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirty-first year, when performing the Bright Hall rites, ceremonial objects were reduced by one third compared with the suburban sacrifice, using 11,500 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirty-first year the Bright Hall rites used ceremonial objects one third fewer than the suburban sacrifice, with an escort of 11,500 men.

sentences.zh: 孝宗隆興二年正月，以鹵簿勞民，乃令有司條具其可省者。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Longxing under Emperor Xiaozong, because the procession insignia burdened the people, the relevant offices were ordered to list item by item what could be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Longxing (1164), Emperor Xiaozong, finding the procession a burden on the people, ordered the relevant offices to list what could be cut.

sentences.zh: 次年郊祀，止用六千八百八十九人，蓋減紹興二十八年人數之半也。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice the following year, only 6,889 men were used—about half the number of the twenty-eighth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice the following year only 6,889 men were used—roughly half the Shaoxing twenty-eighth-year count.

sentences.zh: 乾道六年之郊，雖仍備五輅、大安輦、六象，而人數則如舊焉。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice of the sixth year of Qiandao, although the five chariots, Great Peace Palanquin, and six elephants were still provided, the number of men remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the Qiandao sixth-year suburban sacrifice the five chariots, Great Peace Palanquin, and six elephants were still provided, but personnel remained at the reduced level.

sentences.zh: 自後，終宋之世，雖微有因革，大抵皆如乾道六年之制。

translations.literal: Thereafter, to the end of the Song dynasty, although there were slight changes, on the whole all followed the regulations of the sixth year of Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, until the end of the Song, there were minor adjustments, but the practice largely followed the Qiandao sixth-year model.

sentences.zh: 若明堂，則四輅、大安輦皆省，止用三千三百十九人。

translations.literal: For the Bright Hall, the four chariots and Great Peace Palanquin were all omitted, using only 3,319 men.
translations.idiomatic: For the Bright Hall the four chariots and Great Peace Palanquin were omitted, with only 3,319 men.

sentences.zh: 故事，祀前二日詣景靈宮，皆備大駕儀仗、乘輅。

translations.literal: By precedent, two days before the sacrifice one went to the Palace of Imperial Splendor, fully providing the great imperial ceremonial arms and riding the chariots.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, two days before a sacrifice the emperor visited the Palace of Imperial Splendor with the full great imperial escort and chariots.

sentences.zh: 中興後，以行都與東都不同，前二日止乘輦。

translations.literal: After the restoration, because the traveling capital differed from the Eastern Capital, on the first two days one rode only the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, because the traveling capital differed from the Eastern Capital, on those two days the emperor rode only the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 次日，自太廟詣青城，始登輅，設鹵簿。

translations.literal: The next day, proceeding from the Imperial Ancestral Temple to the Green City, one first mounted the chariot and set out the procession insignia.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, proceeding from the Imperial Ancestral Temple to the Green City, the emperor first mounted the chariot and deployed the procession insignia.

sentences.zh: 自紹興十三年始也。

translations.literal: This began from the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: This practice began in the thirteenth year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 車駕遇雨，玉輅施障，從駕臣僚賜雨具，中道遇晴則撤。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage encountered rain, screens were hung on the jade chariot; accompanying officials were given rain gear; if it cleared midway, they were removed.
translations.idiomatic: When rain fell, screens were hung on the jade chariot, accompanying officials received rain gear, and both were removed if the weather cleared en route.

sentences.zh: 郊壇遇雨，則就青城放禦仗，逍遙子還宮，導駕官免步導。

translations.literal: If rain fell at the suburban altar, the imperial arms escort was dismissed at the Green City, the emperor returned to the palace in the carefree palanquin, and guide officials were excused from foot guidance.
translations.idiomatic: If rain fell at the suburban altar, the imperial escort was dismissed at the Green City, the emperor returned in the carefree palanquin, and guide officials were excused from foot escort.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: Great imperial procession insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Great imperial procession insignia.

sentences.zh: 象六，中道，分左右。

translations.literal: Six elephants, on the central way, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Six elephants on the central way, divided left and right.

sentences.zh: 次六引，中道。

translations.literal: Next, the six sections, on the central way.
translations.idiomatic: Next, the six sections on the central way.

sentences.zh: 第一，開封令；

translations.literal: First, the magistrate of Kaifeng;
translations.idiomatic: First, the magistrate of Kaifeng;

sentences.zh: 第二，開封牧；

translations.literal: second, the prefect of Kaifeng;
translations.idiomatic: second, the prefect of Kaifeng;

sentences.zh: 〈（駕從餘州縣出者，所在刺史、縣令導駕，準此。）〉

translations.literal: (When the imperial carriage departs from other prefectures and counties, the local prefect and magistrate guide the carriage, following this precedent.)
translations.idiomatic: (When the imperial carriage departs from other prefectures and counties, the local prefect and magistrate guide the carriage by this precedent.)

sentences.zh: 第三，太常卿；

translations.literal: third, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: third, the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 第四，司徒；

translations.literal: fourth, the Minister of Education;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the Minister of Education;

sentences.zh: 第五，御史大夫；

translations.literal: fifth, the Censor-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the Censor-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 第六，兵部尚書。

translations.literal: sixth, the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 〈（以上各用本品鹵簿。）〉

translations.literal: (Each of the above uses procession insignia of his proper grade.)
translations.idiomatic: (Each of the above uses procession insignia of his proper grade.)

sentences.zh: 次纛十二。

translations.literal: Next, twelve great banners.
translations.idiomatic: Next, twelve great banners.

sentences.zh: 〈（每纛一人持，一人托，四人扯，騎二人押。）〉

translations.literal: (For each banner, one man holds it, one supports it, four pull it, and two mounted men supervise.)
translations.idiomatic: (Each banner: one bearer, one supporter, four pullers, and two mounted supervisors.)

sentences.zh: 次暴槊騎八，

translations.literal: Next, eight mounted men with bared spears,
translations.idiomatic: Next, eight mounted men with bared spears,

sentences.zh: 〈（押衙四人騎引。）〉

translations.literal: (Four mounted yamen guards lead.)
