sentences.zh: 第二隊，貔旗二，左右領軍衛果毅都尉各一人分領，赤鍪甲、刀盾六十；

translations.literal: Second company: two Pi banners; one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Army-leading Guards commands separately, red-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;
translations.idiomatic: The second company bore two Pi banners, each side led by one Army-leading Guard Resolute Valor commandant with red-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;

sentences.zh: 第三隊，玉馬旗二，左右領軍衛折衝都尉各一人分領，青鍪甲、弓箭六十；

translations.literal: Third company: two jade-horse banners; one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each of the Left and Right Army-leading Guards commands separately, green-crested armor and sixty bowmen;
translations.idiomatic: The third company bore two jade-horse banners, each side led by one Army-leading Guard Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant with green-crested armor and sixty archers;

sentences.zh: 第四隊，三角獸旗二，左右領軍衛果毅都尉各一人分領，青鍪甲、刀盾六十；

translations.literal: Fourth company: two triangular-beast banners; one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Army-leading Guards commands separately, green-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth company bore two triangular-beast banners, each side led by one Army-leading Guard Resolute Valor commandant with green-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;

sentences.zh: 第五隊，黃鹿旗二，左右屯衛折衝都尉各一人分領，黑鍪甲、弓箭六十；

translations.literal: Fifth company: two yellow-deer banners; one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each of the Left and Right Garrison Guards commands separately, black-crested armor and sixty bowmen;
translations.idiomatic: The fifth company bore two yellow-deer banners, each side led by one Garrison Guard Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant with black-crested armor and sixty archers;

sentences.zh: 第六隊，飛麟旗二，左右屯衛果毅都尉各一人分領，黑鍪甲、刀盾六十；

translations.literal: Sixth company: two flying-qilin banners; one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Garrison Guards commands separately, black-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;
translations.idiomatic: The sixth company bore two flying-qilin banners, each side led by one Garrison Guard Resolute Valor commandant with black-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;

sentences.zh: 第七隊，駃騠旗二，左右武衛折衝都尉各一人分領，白鍪甲、弓箭六十；

translations.literal: Seventh company: two swift-camel banners; one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each of the Left and Right Martial Guards commands separately, white-crested armor and sixty bowmen;
translations.idiomatic: The seventh company bore two swift-camel banners, each side led by one Martial Guard Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant with white-crested armor and sixty archers;

sentences.zh: 第八隊，鸞旗二，左右武衛果毅都尉各一人分領，白鍪甲、刀盾六十；

translations.literal: Eighth company: two luan banners; one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Martial Guards commands separately, white-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;
translations.idiomatic: The eighth company bore two luan banners, each side led by one Martial Guard Resolute Valor commandant with white-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;

sentences.zh: 第九隊，麟旗二，左右驍衛折衝都尉各一人分領，黃鍪甲、弓箭六十；

translations.literal: Ninth company: two qilin banners; one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each of the Left and Right Valiant Guards commands separately, yellow-crested armor and sixty bowmen;
translations.idiomatic: The ninth company bore two qilin banners, each side led by one Valiant Guard Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant with yellow-crested armor and sixty archers;

sentences.zh: 第十隊，馴象旗二，左右驍衛果毅都尉各一人分領，黃鍪甲、刀盾六十；

translations.literal: Tenth company: two tame-elephant banners; one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Valiant Guards commands separately, yellow-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;
translations.idiomatic: The tenth company bore two tame-elephant banners, each side led by one Valiant Guard Resolute Valor commandant with yellow-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers;

sentences.zh: 第十一隊，玉兔旗二，左右衛折衝都尉各一人分領，黃鍪甲、弓箭六十；

translations.literal: Eleventh company: two jade-hare banners; one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each of the Left and Right Guards commands separately, yellow-crested armor and sixty bowmen;
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh company bore two jade-hare banners, each side led by one Imperial Guard Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant with yellow-crested armor and sixty archers;

sentences.zh: 第十二隊，辟邪旗二，左右衛果毅都尉各一人分領，黃鍪甲、刀盾六十。

translations.literal: Twelfth company: two ward-off-evil banners; one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Guards commands separately, yellow-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth company bore two ward-off-evil banners, each side led by one Imperial Guard Resolute Valor commandant with yellow-crested armor and sixty sword-and-shield bearers.

sentences.zh: 次前部黃麾仗。

translations.literal: Next, the forward yellow-banner ceremonial arms.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the forward yellow-banner ceremonial escort.

translations.literal: (Left and right ways.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the left and right ways.)

sentences.zh: 絳引幡二十；

translations.literal: Twenty scarlet guide-banners;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty scarlet guide-banners led the way;

sentences.zh: 第一部，左右領軍衛大將軍各一人檢校，

translations.literal: First section: one grand general each of the Left and Right Army-leading Guards inspects,
translations.idiomatic: The first section was inspected by one Army-leading Guard grand general on each side,

sentences.zh: 〈（兼檢校第二部。）〉

translations.literal: (Also inspecting the second section.)
translations.idiomatic: (Also supervising the second section.)

sentences.zh: 折衝都尉各一人分領，

translations.literal: One Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each commands separately,
translations.idiomatic: with one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant commanding each side,

sentences.zh: 〈（主帥二人。）〉

translations.literal: (Two squad leaders.)
translations.idiomatic: (Two squad leaders in all.)

sentences.zh: 龍頭竿赤氅二十，揭鼓二，儀鍠五色幢二十，龍頭竿小孔雀氅二十，小戟二十，揭鼓二，龍頭竿五色鵝毛氅二十，弓箭二十，龍頭雞毛氅二十，朱縢盾二十，龍頭竿繡氅二十，弓箭二十，槊二十，揭鼓二，綠縢盾二十；

translations.literal: Twenty dragon-head poles with red canopies, two signaling drums, twenty ceremonial axe-staff five-color pennants, twenty dragon-head poles with small peacock canopies, twenty small halberds, two signaling drums, twenty dragon-head poles with five-color goose-feather canopies, twenty bowmen, twenty dragon-head poles with chicken-feather canopies, twenty vermillion-cord shields, twenty dragon-head poles with embroidered canopies, twenty bowmen, twenty spears, two signaling drums, twenty green-cord shields;
translations.idiomatic: The section included twenty red-canopied dragon-head poles, two signaling drums, twenty five-color ceremonial axe-staff pennants, twenty small-peacock canopies on dragon-head poles, twenty small halberds, another pair of drums, twenty five-color goose-feather canopies, twenty archers, twenty chicken-feather canopies, twenty vermillion-cord shields, twenty embroidered canopies, twenty more archers, twenty spears, two more drums, and twenty green-cord shields;

sentences.zh: 第二部，左右領軍衛折衝都尉各一人分領；

translations.literal: Second section: one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each of the Left and Right Army-leading Guards commands separately;
translations.idiomatic: The second section was led on each side by one Army-leading Guard Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant;

sentences.zh: 〈（主帥及氅鍠等並同第一部，餘準此。）〉

translations.literal: (Squad leaders, canopies, axe-staffs, and the rest all same as the first section; remaining sections follow this.)
translations.idiomatic: (Squad leaders, canopies, axe-staffs, and the rest matched the first section; the remaining sections followed the same pattern.)

sentences.zh: 第三部，左右屯衛大將軍各一人檢校，果毅都尉各一人分領；

translations.literal: Third section: one grand general each of the Left and Right Garrison Guards inspects, one Resolute Valor commandant each commands separately;
translations.idiomatic: The third section was inspected by one Garrison Guard grand general on each side and led by one Resolute Valor commandant per side;

sentences.zh: 第四部，左右武衛大將軍各一人檢校，折衝都尉各一人分領；

translations.literal: Fourth section: one grand general each of the Left and Right Martial Guards inspects, one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each commands separately;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth section was inspected by one Martial Guard grand general on each side and led by one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant per side;

sentences.zh: 第五部，左右驍衛大將軍各一人檢校；

translations.literal: Fifth section: one grand general each of the Left and Right Valiant Guards inspects;
translations.idiomatic: The fifth section was inspected by one Valiant Guard grand general on each side;

sentences.zh: 〈（兼檢校第六部，折衝都尉各一人分領。）〉

translations.literal: (Also inspecting the sixth section; one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant each commands separately.)
translations.idiomatic: (Also supervising the sixth section, with one Breaker-of-the-Enemy commandant commanding each side.)

sentences.zh: 第六部，左右衛果毅都尉各一人分領。

translations.literal: Sixth section: one Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Guards commands separately.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth section was led on each side by one Imperial Guard Resolute Valor commandant.

sentences.zh: 次六軍儀仗。

translations.literal: Next, the Six Armies ceremonial arms.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Six Armies ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 〈（中道，在殿中黃麾後。）〉

translations.literal: (Central way, behind the Palace yellow banner.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the central way, behind the Palace yellow banner.)

sentences.zh: 左右神武軍統軍各一人，本軍旗二，

translations.literal: One army commander each of the Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, two banners of the native army each,
translations.idiomatic: One commander each of the Left and Right Divine Martial Armies, with two native-army banners apiece,

sentences.zh: 〈（一人執，一人引，二人夾，都頭各一人騎押。）〉

translations.literal: (One man holds, one guides, two flank; one squad chief each rides to escort.)
translations.idiomatic: (One bearer, one guide, and two flankers per banner, each escorted by a mounted squad chief.)

sentences.zh: 吏兵、力士旗各五，白幹槍五十，柯舒十，鐙仗八，

translations.literal: Five clerk-soldier banners and five strongman banners each, fifty white-shafted spears, ten Ke Shu poles, eight stirrup staves,
translations.idiomatic: five clerk-soldier and five strongman banners apiece, fifty white-shafted spears, ten Ke Shu poles, and eight stirrup staves,

translations.literal: (Alternating.)
translations.idiomatic: (Arranged in alternation.)

sentences.zh: 排闌旗二十，掩尾天馬旗二。

translations.literal: Twenty barrier-line banners and two trailing heavenly-horse banners.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty barrier-line banners and two trailing heavenly-horse banners followed.

sentences.zh: 左右羽林軍、左右龍武軍，並同神武軍。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies and the Left and Right Dragon Martial Armies all follow the Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Feathered Forest and Dragon Martial Armies followed the same arrangement as the Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 〈（惟羽林用赤豹、黃熊旗各五，龍武用龍君、虎君旗各五。）〉

translations.literal: (Only the Feathered Forest uses five red-leopard and five yellow-bear banners each; the Dragon Martial uses five dragon-lord and five tiger-lord banners each.)
translations.idiomatic: (Only the Feathered Forest added five red-leopard and five yellow-bear banners apiece; the Dragon Martial added five dragon-lord and five tiger-lord banners apiece.)

sentences.zh: 次引駕旗十六，

translations.literal: Next, sixteen imperial escort banners,
translations.idiomatic: Next came sixteen imperial escort banners,

sentences.zh: 〈（中道，執人同六軍旗。）〉

translations.literal: (Central way; bearers same as Six Armies banners.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the central way, with bearers arranged like the Six Armies banners.)

sentences.zh: 十二辰旗各一，天王旗四。

translations.literal: One Twelve Branches banner each and four heavenly-king banners.
translations.idiomatic: one banner for each of the Twelve Branches and four heavenly-king banners.

sentences.zh: 〈（排仗通直官二人騎領。）〉

translations.literal: (Two formation-arrangement direct-attendant officials ride to lead.)
translations.idiomatic: (Led by two mounted formation-arrangement direct-attendant officials.)

sentences.zh: 次龍墀旗十三，

translations.literal: Next, thirteen Dragon Court banners,
translations.idiomatic: Next came thirteen Dragon Court banners,

sentences.zh: 〈（中道，各一人執，二人引，二人夾，排仗將二人騎領。）〉

translations.literal: (Central way; for each one man holds, two guide, two flank; two formation-arrangement generals ride to lead.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the central way, each banner had one bearer, two guides, and two flankers, led by two mounted formation-arrangement generals.)

sentences.zh: 天下太平旗一，青龍、赤龍、黃龍、白龍、黑龍旗各一，金鸞、金鳳旗各一，獅子旗二，日旗、月旗各一，君王萬歲旗一。

translations.literal: One All Under Heaven at Peace banner; one Azure Dragon, one Vermilion Dragon, one Yellow Dragon, one White Dragon, and one Black Dragon banner each; one Golden Luan and one Golden Phoenix banner each; two lion banners; one sun banner and one moon banner each; one Myriad Years to the Sovereign banner.
translations.idiomatic: There followed one All Under Heaven at Peace banner; one banner each for the azure, vermilion, yellow, white, and black dragons; one Golden Luan and one Golden Phoenix banner; two lion banners; one sun and one moon banner; and one Myriad Years to the Sovereign banner.

sentences.zh: 次御馬二十四匹，

translations.literal: Next, twenty-four imperial horses,
translations.idiomatic: Next came twenty-four imperial horses,

sentences.zh: 〈（中道，並以天武官二人執轡。）〉

translations.literal: (Central way; all with two Heavenly Martial officials holding the reins.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the central way, each horse's reins were held by two Heavenly Martial officials.)

sentences.zh: 尚乘奉御二人從。

translations.literal: Two Palace Transport attendants follow.
translations.idiomatic: Two Palace Transport attendants followed behind.

sentences.zh: 次日月合璧旗一，次苣文旗二，次五星連珠旗一，次祥雲旗二。

translations.literal: Next, one Sun-Moon Combined Disk banner; next, two jade-pattern banners; next, one Five Stars in Alignment banner; next, two auspicious-cloud banners.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one Sun-Moon Combined Disk banner, then two jade-pattern banners, one Five Stars in Alignment banner, and two auspicious-cloud banners.

sentences.zh: 〈（以上並一人執，二人引，二人夾，佩橫刀，執弓箭。）〉

translations.literal: (All above: one man holds, two guide, two flank, wearing horizontal sword and holding bow and arrows.)
translations.idiomatic: (For all the above, one bearer, two guides, and two flankers wore horizontal swords and carried bows and arrows.)

sentences.zh: 次長壽幢一。

translations.literal: Next, one longevity pennant.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one longevity pennant.

sentences.zh: 次青龍、白虎旗各一。

translations.literal: Next, one Azure Dragon banner and one White Tiger banner each.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one Azure Dragon banner and one White Tiger banner.

translations.literal: (Left and right ways.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the left and right ways.)

sentences.zh: 左右衛果毅都尉各一人分領七十騎，弩八，弓箭二十二，槊四十。

translations.literal: One Resolute Valor commandant each of the Left and Right Guards commands separately seventy horsemen, eight crossbows, twenty-two bowmen, and forty spearmen.
translations.idiomatic: One Imperial Guard Resolute Valor commandant commanded each side with seventy horsemen, eight crossbowmen, twenty-two archers, and forty spearmen.

sentences.zh: 次班劍儀刀隊。

translations.literal: Next, the court-sword ceremonial-blade company.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the court-sword and ceremonial-blade company.

translations.literal: (Left and right ways.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the left and right ways.)

sentences.zh: 左右衛將軍各一人，親衛郎將各二人，班劍二百二十，為第一、第二行；

translations.literal: One general each of the Left and Right Guards, two personal guard lieutenant-generals each, two hundred twenty court swords, forming the first and second ranks;
translations.idiomatic: One Imperial Guard general on each side, two personal guard lieutenant-generals apiece, and two hundred twenty court swords formed the first and second ranks;

sentences.zh: 勳衛郎將各二人，班劍二百二十，為第三、第四行；

translations.literal: Two Merit Guard lieutenant-generals each, two hundred twenty court swords, forming the third and fourth ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Two Merit Guard lieutenant-generals apiece and two hundred twenty court swords formed the third and fourth ranks;

sentences.zh: 翊衛郎將各三人，儀刀三百七十八，為第五、第六、第七行；

translations.literal: Three Palace Attendant Guard lieutenant-generals each, three hundred seventy-eight ceremonial blades, forming the fifth, sixth, and seventh ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Three Palace Attendant Guard lieutenant-generals apiece, three hundred seventy-eight ceremonial blades, and the fifth, sixth, and seventh ranks;

sentences.zh: 左右驍衛翊衛郎將各一人，儀刀一百三十四，為第八行；

translations.literal: One Valiant Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general each of left and right, one hundred thirty-four ceremonial blades, forming the eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Valiant Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general on each side and one hundred thirty-four ceremonial blades formed the eighth rank;

sentences.zh: 左右武衛翊衛郎將各一人，儀刀一百三十八，為第九行；

translations.literal: One Martial Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general each of left and right, one hundred thirty-eight ceremonial blades, forming the ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Martial Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general on each side and one hundred thirty-eight ceremonial blades formed the ninth rank;

sentences.zh: 左右屯衛翊衛郎將各一人，儀刀一百四十二，為第十行；

translations.literal: One Garrison Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general each of left and right, one hundred forty-two ceremonial blades, forming the tenth rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Garrison Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general on each side and one hundred forty-two ceremonial blades formed the tenth rank;

sentences.zh: 左右領軍衛翊衛郎將各一人，儀刀一百四十六，為第十一行；

translations.literal: One Army-leading Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general each of left and right, one hundred forty-six ceremonial blades, forming the eleventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: One Army-leading Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general on each side and one hundred forty-six ceremonial blades formed the eleventh rank;

sentences.zh: 左右金吾衛翊衛郎將各一人，儀刀一百五十，為第十二行。

translations.literal: One Golden Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general each of left and right, one hundred fifty ceremonial blades, forming the twelfth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One Golden Guard Palace Attendant lieutenant-general on each side and one hundred fifty ceremonial blades formed the twelfth rank.

sentences.zh: 次五仗。

translations.literal: Next, the Five Guards arms.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Five Guards ceremonial arms.

translations.literal: (Left and right ways.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the left and right ways.)

sentences.zh: 左右衛供奉中郎將各二人，親勳翊衛各二十四人，左右衛郎將各一人，散手翊衛各三十人，左右驍衛郎將各一人，翊衛各二十八人。

translations.literal: Two palace-attending central commander-generals each of the Left and Right Guards, twenty-four personal merit palace attendants each, one Imperial Guard lieutenant-general each of left and right, thirty unattached palace attendants each, one Valiant Guard lieutenant-general each of left and right, and twenty-eight palace attendants each.
translations.idiomatic: Two palace-attending central commander-generals from each Imperial Guard, twenty-four personal merit palace attendants apiece, one Imperial Guard lieutenant-general on each side, thirty unattached palace attendants each, one Valiant Guard lieutenant-general per side, and twenty-eight palace attendants each followed.

sentences.zh: 次左右驍衛、翊衛三隊。

translations.literal: Next, three companies of the Left and Right Valiant Guard and Palace Attendant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three companies from the Valiant Guard and Palace Attendant Guard on left and right.

sentences.zh: 第一隊，花鳳旗二，大將軍各一人，弩十，弓箭二十，槊四十；

translations.literal: First company: two flower-phoenix banners, one grand general each, ten crossbows, twenty bows and arrows, forty spears;
translations.idiomatic: The first company had two flower-phoenix banners, one grand general each, ten crossbowmen, twenty archers, and forty spearmen;

sentences.zh: 第二隊，飛黃旗二，將軍各一人，

translations.literal: Second company: two Flying Yellow banners, one general each,
translations.idiomatic: The second company had two Flying Yellow banners and one general each,

sentences.zh: 〈（弩、弓箭、槊同第一隊，下準此。）〉

translations.literal: (Crossbows, bows and arrows, and spears same as the first company; below follows this precedent.)
translations.idiomatic: (Crossbows, archers, and spearmen as in the first company; the same rule applies below.)

sentences.zh: 第三隊，吉利旗二，郎將各一人。

translations.literal: Third company: two auspicious banners, one lieutenant-general each.
translations.idiomatic: The third company had two auspicious banners, each led by a lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 次金吾細仗。

translations.literal: Next, the Golden Guard detailed arms.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Golden Guard detailed arms escort.

sentences.zh: 殿中傘扇，千牛。

translations.literal: Palace Directorate umbrellas and fans; Thousand-Ox.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Directorate supplied umbrellas and fans, with the Thousand-Ox Guard.

translations.literal: (Central way.)
translations.idiomatic: (On the central way.)

sentences.zh: 青龍、白虎旗各一，

translations.literal: One Azure Dragon banner and one White Tiger banner each,
translations.idiomatic: one Azure Dragon banner and one White Tiger banner followed,

sentences.zh: 〈（一人執，三人引，騎二人押當。）〉

translations.literal: (One man holds, three guide, two mounted men supervise.)
translations.idiomatic: (One bearer, three guides, and two mounted supervisors.)

sentences.zh: 五嶽神旗各一，五方神旗各一，五方龍旗二十五，五方鳳旗二十五，四瀆神旗各一。

translations.literal: One Five Sacred Mountains spirit banner each, one Five Directions spirit banner each, twenty-five Five Directions dragon banners, twenty-five Five Directions phoenix banners, and one Four Rivers spirit banner each.
translations.idiomatic: There followed banners for the Five Sacred Mountains and Five Directions, twenty-five dragon and twenty-five phoenix banners for the five directions, and one banner for each of the Four Rivers.

sentences.zh: 〈（各一人執，二人引，二人夾，四旗屬兵部，每行次五方鳳旗。）〉

translations.literal: (For each one man holds, two guide, two flank; the four banners belong to the Ministry of War; in each rank the Five Directions phoenix banners are placed next.)

translations.idiomatic: (These totaled five hundred four men from the inner enclosure through the mobile palace Quick-Step posts.)

sentences.zh: 凡詣小次行禮，隨從祗應。

translations.literal: Whenever proceeding to the minor rest pavilion to perform rites, attendants waited upon.
translations.idiomatic: When proceeding to the minor rest pavilion to perform rites, attendants were required to wait upon the emperor.

sentences.zh: 圓壇從外壝下分作九重：從中第一重，殿前指揮使等七百四十四人；

translations.literal: The round altar from below the outer enclosure was divided into nine rings: from the center, the first ring, Palace Front commanders and others seven hundred forty-four men;
translations.idiomatic: From below the outer enclosure, the round altar was divided into nine rings: the innermost ring held seven hundred forty-four Palace Front commanders and others;

sentences.zh: 第二重，禦龍直等六百九十五人；

translations.literal: Second ring, Imperial Dragon Direct and others six hundred ninety-five men;
translations.idiomatic: the second ring, six hundred ninety-five Imperial Dragon Direct guards and others;

sentences.zh: 第三重，散員等六百四十二人；

translations.literal: Third ring, Unattached members and others six hundred forty-two men;
translations.idiomatic: the third ring, six hundred forty-two Unattached Members and others;

sentences.zh: 第四重，散都頭等七百一十人；

translations.literal: Fourth ring, Unattached squad chiefs and others seven hundred ten men;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth ring, seven hundred ten Unattached Squad Chiefs and others;

sentences.zh: 第五重，天武骨朵大劍約攔五百八十一人；

translations.literal: Fifth ring, Heavenly Martial mace, great sword, and cordon five hundred eighty-one men;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth ring, five hundred eighty-one Heavenly Martial mace, great-sword, and cordon guards;

sentences.zh: 第六重，御營四面巡檢下步軍八百六十七人；

translations.literal: Sixth ring, Imperial Camp Four-Directions inspectors' foot soldiers eight hundred sixty-seven men;
translations.idiomatic: the sixth ring, eight hundred sixty-seven foot soldiers under the Imperial Camp Four-Directions inspectors;

sentences.zh: 第七重，御營四面並青城圓壇巡檢下步軍八百六十七人；

translations.literal: Seventh ring, Imperial Camp Four-Directions and Green City round-altar inspectors' foot soldiers eight hundred sixty-seven men;
translations.idiomatic: the seventh ring, eight hundred sixty-seven foot soldiers under the Imperial Camp Four-Directions and Green City round-altar inspectors;

sentences.zh: 第八重，御營四面巡檢下馬軍四百三十三人；

translations.literal: Eighth ring, Imperial Camp Four-Directions inspectors' mounted soldiers four hundred thirty-three men;
translations.idiomatic: the eighth ring, four hundred thirty-three mounted soldiers under the Imperial Camp Four-Directions inspectors;

sentences.zh: 第九重，御營四面巡檢及青城圓壇巡檢下馬軍四百三十四人。

translations.literal: Ninth ring, Imperial Camp Four-Directions inspectors and Green City round-altar inspectors' mounted soldiers four hundred thirty-four men.
translations.idiomatic: the ninth ring, four hundred thirty-four mounted soldiers under the Imperial Camp Four-Directions and Green City round-altar inspectors.

sentences.zh: 壇四門殿前指揮使行門三十五人，內人員一十五人，壇東門夾立擎鞭長行一十人。

translations.literal: At the altar's four gates, Palace Front commanders gate duty thirty-five men, inner personnel fifteen men; flanking the altar's eastern gate stood ten long-service whip-bearers.
translations.idiomatic: At the altar's four gates were thirty-five Palace Front gate guards and fifteen inner personnel; ten long-service whip bearers flanked the altar's eastern gate.

sentences.zh: 〈（右自青城赴壇諸班親從文武及御營圓壇巡檢下，總七千四百六十七人。）〉

translations.literal: (In all, from the Green City to the altar, various direct companies' personal attendants, civil and military, and Imperial Camp round-altar inspectors' subordinates totaled seven thousand four hundred sixty-seven men.)
translations.idiomatic: (In all, from the Green City to the altar—including personal attendants from the various direct companies, civil and military officials, and subordinates of the Imperial Camp round-altar inspectors—the total was seven thousand four hundred sixty-seven men.)

sentences.zh: 駕至太廟，環衛如郊壇，坐甲布列二百六十三鋪。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached the Imperial Ancestral Temple, encircling guard was as at the suburban altar, with armored guards seated in deployment at two hundred sixty-three posts.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the encircling guard followed the suburban-altar model, with armored guards posted at two hundred sixty-three stations.

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使二十四鋪，四百七十七人；

translations.literal: Palace Front commanders twenty-four posts, four hundred seventy-seven men;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four Palace Front stations with four hundred seventy-seven men;

sentences.zh: 內殿直、散員、散指揮、散都頭、散祗候、散直各一十鋪，一百二十人，共六十鋪七百二十人；

translations.literal: Inner Palace Direct, Unattached members, Unattached commanders, Unattached squad chiefs, Unattached palace attendants, and Unattached Direct each ten posts, one hundred twenty men, totaling sixty posts and seven hundred twenty men;
translations.idiomatic: Inner Palace Direct, Unattached Members, Unattached Commanders, Unattached Squad Chiefs, Unattached Palace Attendants, and Unattached Direct each had ten stations of one hundred twenty men, sixty stations in all with seven hundred twenty men;

sentences.zh: 金槍一十鋪，一百五十人；

translations.literal: Golden Lance ten posts, one hundred fifty men;
translations.idiomatic: ten Golden Lance stations with one hundred fifty men;

sentences.zh: 銀槍一十鋪，一百五十人；

translations.literal: Silver Lance ten posts, one hundred fifty men;
translations.idiomatic: ten Silver Lance stations with one hundred fifty men;

sentences.zh: 東第一、第二班各二鋪，三十人，共四鋪，六十人；

translations.literal: East First and Second Shifts each two posts, thirty men, totaling four posts and sixty men;
translations.idiomatic: East First and Second Shifts each had two stations of thirty men, four stations and sixty men in all;

sentences.zh: 東第三、第四班各四鋪，六十人，共八鋪，一百二十人；

translations.literal: East Third and Fourth Shifts each four posts, sixty men, totaling eight posts and one hundred twenty men;
translations.idiomatic: East Third and Fourth Shifts each had four stations of sixty men, eight stations and one hundred twenty men in all;

sentences.zh: 東第五班二鋪，二十二人；

translations.literal: East Fifth Shift two posts, twenty-two men;
translations.idiomatic: two East Fifth Shift stations with twenty-two men;

sentences.zh: 下茶酒班一鋪，三十一人；

translations.literal: Lower Tea and Wine Shift one post, thirty-one men;
translations.idiomatic: one Lower Tea and Wine Shift station with thirty-one men;

sentences.zh: 禦龍直八鋪，三百八十五人；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Direct: eight sections, 385 men;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Dragon Direct comprised eight sections with 385 men;

sentences.zh: 禦龍骨朵子直四鋪，二百一十二人，禦龍弓箭直六鋪，二百九十六人；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Staff Direct: four sections, 212 men; Imperial Dragon Bow-and-Arrow Direct: six sections, 296 men;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Staff Direct, four sections and 212 men; Imperial Dragon Bow-and-Arrow Direct, six sections and 296 men;

sentences.zh: 禦龍弩直八鋪，三百五十六人；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct: eight sections, 356 men;
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct comprised eight sections with 356 men;

sentences.zh: 把行門天武一鋪，八人；

translations.literal: Gate-keeping Heavenly Martial: one section, eight men;
translations.idiomatic: Gate-keeping Heavenly Martial had one section of eight men;

sentences.zh: 駕頭扇筤天武一鋪，三十二人；

translations.literal: Carriage-head Fan-rack Heavenly Martial: one section, thirty-two men;
translations.idiomatic: Carriage-head and fan-rack Heavenly Martial: one section, thirty-two men;

sentences.zh: 禁衛天武六鋪，三百一十人；

translations.literal: Palace Guard Heavenly Martial: six sections, 310 men;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard Heavenly Martial numbered six sections with 310 men;

sentences.zh: 禁衛崇政殿親從四十鋪，並提舉人員共四百六十三人；

translations.literal: Palace Guard Chongzheng Hall personal followers: forty sections, together with supervising personnel totaling 463 men;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard personal followers of Chongzheng Hall: forty sections, with supervising personnel totaling 463 men;

sentences.zh: 行宮司親從一十二鋪，一百八十人；

translations.literal: Traveling Palace Office personal followers: twelve sections, 180 men;
translations.idiomatic: The Traveling Palace Office fielded twelve sections of personal followers, 180 men;

sentences.zh: 快行親從四鋪，八十六人；

translations.literal: Rapid-march personal followers: four sections, 86 men;
translations.idiomatic: Rapid-march personal followers totaled four sections with 86 men;

sentences.zh: 方圍親從二十四鋪，三百六十人；

translations.literal: Square-perimeter personal followers: twenty-four sections, 360 men;
translations.idiomatic: Square-perimeter personal followers comprised twenty-four sections with 360 men;

sentences.zh: 約攔天武三十鋪，三百一十人。

translations.literal: Intercepting Heavenly Martial: thirty sections, 310 men.
translations.idiomatic: Street-intercepting Heavenly Martial: thirty sections, 310 men.

sentences.zh: 行宮殿門崇政殿親從及提舉人員二百八十六人，把街約攔親事官貼諸處齪門一十二隊，並提舉人員一百三人，御營四面巡檢六員下步軍九百一十八人，親從四十人。

translations.literal: Traveling palace gate and Chongzheng Hall personal followers and supervising personnel: 286 men; street-intercepting personal-affairs officials posted at various barrier gates: twelve detachments, with supervising personnel 103 men; under the six inspectors of the four sides of the imperial camp, foot soldiers 918 men, personal followers 40 men.
translations.idiomatic: At the traveling palace gates, Chongzheng Hall personal followers and supervisors numbered 286; street-intercepting personal-affairs officials at various barrier gates formed twelve detachments with 103 supervisors; under six inspectors on all sides of the imperial camp were 918 foot soldiers and 40 personal followers.

sentences.zh: 青城內至圜壇巡檢下親從四十人。

translations.literal: Within the Green City to the round altar, under the patrol inspectors: 40 personal followers.
translations.idiomatic: From within the Green City to the round altar, patrol inspectors had 40 personal followers.

sentences.zh: 右禁衛諸班直等御營四面巡檢軍兵，及青城至圜壇巡檢下親從，總六千一百四十五人。

translations.literal: The palace guard direct companies and the like, imperial camp four-side patrol soldiers, and personal followers under patrol from the Green City to the round altar—in all 6,145 men.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard direct companies, four-side imperial-camp patrol troops, and personal followers from the Green City to the round altar totaled 6,145 men.

sentences.zh: 〈（左山商氏家藏宋人《青城》、《圜壇》、《太廟》三圖，其布置行列，極為詳備，因附鹵簿之後，庶覽之者可以考一代之制雲。）〉

translations.literal: (The Shang family of Zuoshan possesses three Song-dynasty diagrams—Green City, Round Altar, and Imperial Ancestral Temple—their arrangements and ranks extremely detailed. They are therefore appended after the procession insignia, so that viewers may examine the regulations of an age.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Shang family of Zuoshan preserves three Song diagrams—the Green City, Round Altar, and Imperial Ancestral Temple—with extremely detailed formations. They are appended after the procession insignia so readers may study the regulations of the dynasty.)

sentences.zh: 凡鹵簿內牙門旗，中道四，分二門；

translations.literal: In all, within the procession insignia, gate-banner flags: on the central way four, divided into two gates;
translations.idiomatic: Within the procession, gate-banner flags on the central way numbered four, forming two gates;

sentences.zh: 左右道各十，分五門。

translations.literal: on the left and right ways ten each, divided into five gates.
translations.idiomatic: on the left and right ways ten each, forming five gates.

sentences.zh: 中道一門在金吾細仗前，一門在掩後隊後。

translations.literal: On the central way, one gate was before the Golden Guard fine arms; one gate was after the covering rear detachment.
translations.idiomatic: On the central way one gate stood before the Golden Guard fine arms and one after the covering rear detachment.

sentences.zh: 左右廂第一門在步甲前隊第六後，第二門在前部黃麾仗前，第三門在後部黃麾仗前，第四門在黃麾仗後，第五門在步甲後隊第六後。

translations.literal: On the left and right flanks, the first gate was after the sixth of the foot-armor front detachment; the second gate before the front yellow-banner arms; the third gate before the rear yellow-banner arms; the fourth gate after the yellow-banner arms; the fifth gate after the sixth of the foot-armor rear detachment.
translations.idiomatic: On the left and right flanks the first gate followed the sixth rank of the foot-armor front detachment; the second stood before the front yellow-banner arms; the third before the rear yellow-banner arms; the fourth after the yellow-banner arms; and the fifth after the sixth rank of the foot-armor rear detachment.

sentences.zh: 每旗二人執，四人夾，並騎，分左右。

translations.literal: For each flag two men held it, four flanked it, all mounted, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Each flag had two bearers and four flankers, all mounted, divided left and right.

sentences.zh: 每門監門校尉六人領。

translations.literal: For each gate six gate-keeping company commanders led.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate was led by six gate-keeping company commanders.

sentences.zh: 又大駕，郊祀、籍田、薦獻玉清昭應景靈宮用之。

translations.literal: Again, the great imperial carriage was used for suburban sacrifice, ploughing the sacred field, and presenting offerings at the Palaces of Jade Purity, Blessing and Response, and Imperial Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The great imperial procession was used for suburban sacrifice, ploughing the sacred field, and offerings at the Palaces of Jade Purity, Blessing and Response, and Imperial Splendor.

sentences.zh: 迎奉聖像亦用大駕，惟不設象及六引導駕官。

translations.literal: Welcoming and escorting sacred images also used the great imperial carriage, only without elephants and the six sections of officials guiding the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming sacred images also used the great imperial procession, but without elephants or the six sections of guide officials.

sentences.zh: 法駕，減太常卿、司徒、兵部尚書，白鷺、崇德車，大輦、五副輅，進賢、明遠車，又減屬車四，餘並三分減一。

translations.literal: The statutory carriage omitted the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Minister of Education, and Minister of War; the White Egret and Honoring Virtue carriages; the great palanquin and five attendant chariots; the Advancing the Worthy and Bright Distance carriages; and four attendant chariots were further reduced—the remainder all reduced by one third.
translations.idiomatic: The statutory procession omitted the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director, Minister of Education, and Minister of War; the White Egret and Honoring Virtue carriages; the great palanquin and five attendant chariots; the Advancing the Worthy and Bright Distance carriages; and four more attendant chariots—with all remaining elements reduced by one third.

sentences.zh: 泰山下、汾陰行禮，明堂、大慶殿恭謝用之，凡一萬一千八十八人。

translations.literal: It was used for performing rites below Mount Tai and at Fenyin, and for expressing gratitude at the Bright Hall and Hall of Great Celebration—in all 11,088 men.
translations.idiomatic: It was used for rites at Mount Tai and Fenyin and for thanksgiving at the Bright Hall and Hall of Great Celebration, with 11,088 men in all.

sentences.zh: 鸞駕，又減縣令、州牧、御史大夫，指南、記裏、鸞旗、皮軒車，象輅、革輅、木輅，耕根車、羊車、黃鉞車、豹尾車、屬車，小輦、小輿，餘並減半。

translations.literal: The luan carriage further omitted the magistrate, prefect, and Censor-in-chief; the compass, mile-marker, luan banner, and leather-canopy carriages; the elephant, leather, and wooden chariots; the Ploughing the Sacred Field, sheep, yellow-axe, and leopard-tail carriages and attendant chariots; the small palanquin and small carrying-chair—the remainder all reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: The luan procession further omitted the magistrate, prefect, and Censor-in-chief; compass, mile-marker, luan banner, and leather-canopy carriages; elephant, leather, and wooden chariots; Ploughing the Sacred Field, sheep, yellow-axe, and leopard-tail carriages and attendants; and the small palanquin and carrying-chair—with everything else cut in half.

sentences.zh: 朝陵，迎泰山天書，東封、西祀，朝謁太清宮，奏告玉清昭應宮，奉迎刻玉天書，躬謝太廟，皆用之。

translations.literal: It was used for visiting imperial tombs; welcoming the Heavenly Book at Mount Tai; the eastern feng and western sacrifice; audience at the Great Pure Palace; memorial reporting at the Palace of Jade Purity and Blessing and Response; escorting the carved-jade Heavenly Book; and personal thanksgiving at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: It was used for tomb visits; welcoming the Heavenly Book at Mount Tai; eastern feng and western sacrifices; audiences at the Great Pure Palace; memorials at the Palace of Jade Purity and Blessing and Response; escorting the carved-jade Heavenly Book; and personal thanksgiving at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 鸞駕舊用二千人，大中祥符五年，真宗告太廟，增至七千人。

translations.literal: The luan carriage formerly used 2,000 men. In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when Emperor Zhenzong reported to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, it was increased to 7,000 men.
translations.idiomatic: The luan procession formerly employed 2,000 men. In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1012), when Emperor Zhenzong reported to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the number rose to 7,000.

sentences.zh: 兵部黃麾仗，用太常鼓吹，太僕寺金玉輅，殿中省大輦，其制無定，然皆減於小駕。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War yellow-banner arms escort used the Court of Imperial Sacrifices wind and percussion, the Court of the Imperial Stud jade and golden chariots, and the Palace Department great palanquin. Its regulations were not fixed, but all were reduced compared with the lesser imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War yellow-banner escort used Court of Imperial Sacrifices wind and percussion, Imperial Stud jade and golden chariots, and Palace Department great palanquin. Its scale was not fixed but always fell below the lesser imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 禦樓、車駕親征或省方還京，迎禁中天書，五嶽上冊，建安軍迎奉聖像，太廟上冊皆用之。

translations.literal: It was used for the imperial tower; when the imperial carriage personally campaigned or returned to the capital after inspecting the provinces; welcoming the Heavenly Book from within the Forbidden City; presenting registers at the Five Sacred Peaks; Jian'an Army welcoming and escorting sacred images; and presenting registers at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: It was used at the imperial tower; when the emperor campaigned in person or returned after touring the provinces; welcoming the Heavenly Book from within the Forbidden City; presenting registers at the Five Sacred Peaks; Jian'an Army escorts of sacred images; and register presentations at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
